bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第194卷卷第一百九十四

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 194, the hundred ninety-fourth volume.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 194.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀十】 起玄黓執徐，盡強圉作噩四月，凡五年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 10] From Xuanji Zhixu through the fourth month of Qiangyu Zuoe; a little more than five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 10] From Xuanji Zhixu through the fourth month of Qiangyu Zuoe—slightly more than five years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the yimao cycle, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of yimao, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，靜州獠反，將軍李子和討平之。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Liao of Jing Prefecture rebelled; General Li Zihe campaigned against them and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the Liao tribes of Jing Prefecture rose in revolt; General Li Zihe marched against them and put the rebellion down.

sentences.zh: 文武官復請封禪，上曰：「卿輩皆以封禪為帝王盛事，朕意不然。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials again requested a Feng and Shan sacrifice. The emperor said, "You all regard Feng and Shan as the great affair of emperors and kings; my mind is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials again petitioned for a Feng and Shan sacrifice. The emperor said, "You all treat Feng and Shan as the supreme ritual of emperors; I do not see it that way.

sentences.zh: 若天下乂安，家給人足，雖不封禪，庸何傷乎！

translations.literal: If the realm is at peace and every household has enough, though one does not perform Feng and Shan, what harm is there!
translations.idiomatic: If the realm is at peace and every household has enough to live on, what harm is there in forgoing Feng and Shan!

sentences.zh: 昔秦始皇封禪，而漢文帝不封禪，後世豈以文帝之賢不及始皇邪！

translations.literal: In former times Qin Shihuang performed Feng and Shan, yet Emperor Wen of Han did not; did later ages deem Wen's worthiness inferior to the First Emperor's!
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang performed Feng and Shan, yet Emperor Wen of Han did not—did later ages judge Wen less worthy than the First Emperor!

sentences.zh: 且事天掃地而祭，何必登泰山之巔，封數尺之土，然後可以展其誠敬乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, in serving Heaven one sweeps the ground and sacrifices—why must one ascend the summit of Mount Tai and seal a few feet of earth before one can display sincerity and reverence!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, one serves Heaven by sweeping the ground and offering sacrifice—why must one climb to the summit of Mount Tai and seal a few feet of earth before sincerity and reverence can be shown!

sentences.zh: 」群臣猶請之不已，上亦欲從之，魏徵獨以為不可。

translations.literal: " The officials still pressed the request without cease; the emperor also wished to comply, but Wei Zheng alone held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: " The officials kept pressing the matter, and the emperor was inclined to agree, but Wei Zheng alone objected.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「公不欲朕封禪者，以功未高邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You do not wish me to perform Feng and Shan—is it because my achievements are not yet lofty?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You oppose my performing Feng and Shan—is it because my achievements are not yet lofty?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「高矣。

translations.literal: " He replied, "They are lofty."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "They are lofty."

sentences.zh: 」「德未厚邪？

translations.literal: " "Is virtue not yet ample?"
translations.idiomatic: " "Is my virtue not yet ample?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「厚矣。

translations.literal: " He replied, "It is ample."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "It is ample."

sentences.zh: 」「中國未安邪？

translations.literal: " "Is the Central Realm not yet at peace?"
translations.idiomatic: " "Is the Central Realm not yet at peace?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「安矣。

translations.literal: " He replied, "It is at peace."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "It is at peace."

sentences.zh: 」「四夷未服邪？

translations.literal: " "Have the four barbarians not yet submitted?"
translations.idiomatic: " "Have the four quarters not yet submitted?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「服矣。

translations.literal: " He replied, "They have submitted."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "They have submitted."

sentences.zh: 」「年谷未豐邪？

translations.literal: " "Are the year's grains not yet abundant?"
translations.idiomatic: " "Are the harvests not yet abundant?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「豐矣。

translations.literal: " He replied, "They are abundant."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "They are abundant."

sentences.zh: 」「符瑞未至邪？

translations.literal: " "Have auspicious omens not yet arrived?"
translations.idiomatic: " "Have auspicious omens not yet appeared?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「至矣。

translations.literal: " He replied, "They have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "They have appeared."

sentences.zh: 」然則何為不可封禪？

translations.literal: " Then why may Feng and Shan not be performed?"
translations.idiomatic: " Then why should Feng and Shan still be impossible?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下雖有此六者，然承隋末大亂之後，戶口未復，倉廩尚虛，而車駕東巡，千乘萬騎，其供頓勞費，未易任也。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Although Your Majesty has these six things, yet coming after the great disorder at the end of Sui, household registers have not been restored and granaries are still empty; if the imperial carriage tours eastward with thousands of chariots and ten thousands of riders, the provisioning and labor costs would not be easy to bear.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Though Your Majesty has these six things, you inherit the aftermath of Sui's final chaos: population registers are not yet restored and granaries remain empty. An eastern tour with thousands of chariots and tens of thousands of horsemen would impose provisioning and labor costs that are hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 且陛下封禪，則萬國咸集，遠夷君長，皆當扈從；

translations.literal: Moreover, if Your Majesty performs Feng and Shan, then the myriad states will all assemble and distant barbarian chieftains must all follow in attendance;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if Your Majesty performs Feng and Shan, all states will gather and distant barbarian rulers will all attend;

sentences.zh: 今自伊、洛以東至於海、岱，煙火尚希，灌莽極目，此乃引戎狄入腹中，示之以虛弱也。

translations.literal: now from the Yi and Luo eastward to the sea and Mount Dai, hearth-fires are still sparse and wild growth stretches to the horizon—this would be leading the Rong and Di into the belly of the realm and showing them its weakness.
translations.idiomatic: from the Yi and Luo eastward to the sea and Mount Dai, hearth-fires are still sparse and wilderness stretches to the horizon—this would invite the barbarians into the heart of the realm and display our weakness.

sentences.zh: 況賞賚不貲，未厭遠人之望；

translations.literal: Moreover rewards and gifts would be beyond reckoning, yet would not satisfy the hopes of men from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and gifts would be beyond reckoning, yet would not satisfy the expectations of distant peoples;

sentences.zh: 給復連年，不償百姓之勞；

translations.literal: tax exemptions year after year would not repay the people's toil;
translations.idiomatic: tax exemptions year after year would not repay the people's labor;

sentences.zh: 崇虛名而受實害，陛下將焉用之！

translations.literal: to exalt empty reputation while suffering real harm—what use would Your Majesty have for that!
translations.idiomatic: to pursue empty glory while suffering real harm—of what use would that be to Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 」會河南、北數州大水，事遂寢。

translations.literal: " Just then several prefectures north and south of the Yellow River suffered great floods, and the matter was laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time several prefectures north and south of the Yellow River were struck by great floods, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 上將幸九成宮，通直散騎常侍姚思廉諫。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to visit Jiucheng Palace; Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unrestricted Cavalry Yao Silian remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to visit Jiucheng Palace, Yao Silian, Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unrestricted Cavalry, remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕有氣疾，暑輒頓劇，往避之耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I have a qi disorder; in summer it suddenly grows severe—I am going only to escape it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I suffer from a respiratory ailment that worsens sharply in summer; I am going only to escape the heat."

sentences.zh: 」賜思廉絹五十匹。

translations.literal: " He bestowed on Silian fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " He rewarded Silian with fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 監察御史馬周上疏，以為：「東宮在宮城之中，而大安宮乃在宮城之西，制度比於宸居，尚為卑小，於四方觀聽，有所不足。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Ma Zhou submitted a memorial, holding that: "The Eastern Palace lies within the palace city, yet Da'an Palace is west of the palace city; though its scale compares with the imperial residence, it is still low and small, and in the eyes and ears of the four quarters this is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Ma Zhou submitted a memorial arguing that the Eastern Palace lies within the palace city while Da'an Palace stands west of it; though its scale compares with the imperial residence, it remains too low and small to satisfy what the realm sees and hears.

sentences.zh: 宜增修高大，以稱中外之望。

translations.literal: It should be enlarged and raised high to match the hopes within and without.
translations.idiomatic: It should be enlarged and raised to match expectations at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 又，太上皇春秋已高，陛下宜朝夕視膳。

translations.literal: Moreover the Retired Emperor's years are already advanced; Your Majesty should attend his meals morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Retired Emperor is advanced in years; Your Majesty should attend his meals morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 今九成宮去京師三百餘里，太上皇或時思念陛下，陛下何以赴之？

translations.literal: Now Jiucheng Palace is more than three hundred li from the capital; if the Retired Emperor at times longs for Your Majesty, how will Your Majesty go to him?
translations.idiomatic: Jiucheng Palace is more than three hundred li from the capital; if the Retired Emperor longs for Your Majesty, how will you reach him?

sentences.zh: 又，車駕此行，欲以避暑；

translations.literal: Moreover this journey of the imperial carriage is meant to escape the heat;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this journey is meant to escape the summer heat;

sentences.zh: 太上皇尚留暑中，而陛下獨居京處，溫清之禮，竊所未安。

translations.literal: the Retired Emperor still remains in the summer heat while Your Majesty alone dwells in the cool—this humble one is privately uneasy about the rites of warmth and coolness.
translations.idiomatic: yet the Retired Emperor remains in the summer heat while Your Majesty enjoys the cool alone—I am uneasy about the breach of filial duty in tending to his comfort.

sentences.zh: 今行計已成，不可復止，願速示返期，以解眾惑。

translations.literal: Now that the journey is already settled and cannot be stopped, I wish Your Majesty would quickly announce the date of return to dispel the multitude's doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Since the journey cannot now be stopped, I ask that Your Majesty announce a date of return at once to dispel public uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 又，王長通、白明達皆樂工，韋槃提、斛斯正止能調馬，縱使技能出眾，正可賚之金帛，豈得超授官爵，鳴玉曳履，與士君子比肩而立，同坐而食？

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Changtong and Bai Mingda are both musicians; Wei Pantuo and Husizheng can only train horses—even if their skills were outstanding, they should merely be rewarded with gold and silk; how can they be promoted beyond measure to offices and ranks, jade sounding at the belt and trailing shoes, standing shoulder to shoulder with gentlemen and scholars and sitting and eating together?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Wang Changtong and Bai Mingda are musicians, and Wei Pantuo and Husizheng can only train horses—even if their skills were outstanding, they deserve no more than gold and silk; how can they be given offices and ranks, jade at the belt and trailing shoes, standing shoulder to shoulder with gentlemen and dining with them?

sentences.zh: 臣竊恥之。

translations.literal: This humble one is privately ashamed of it.
translations.idiomatic: I am ashamed of this.

sentences.zh: 」上深納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted the advice wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 上以新令無三師官，二月，丙戌，詔特置之。

translations.literal: Because the new statutes had no office of the Three Preceptors, in the second month on bingxu an edict specially established them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the new legal code omitted the Three Preceptors, in the second month on bingxu an edict specially re-established the office.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊辰，上幸九成宮。

translations.literal: In the third month on wuchen the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month on wuchen the emperor went to Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 庚午，吐谷渾寇蘭州，州兵擊走之。

translations.literal: On gengwu Tuyuhun raided Lan Prefecture; the prefectural troops struck them and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Tuyuhun raided Lan Prefecture; the prefectural troops repelled them.

sentences.zh: 長樂公主將出降，上以公主皇后所生，特愛之，敕有司資送倍於永嘉長公主。

translations.literal: The Princess of Changle was about to marry out; because the princess was born of the empress the emperor especially loved her and ordered the authorities to provide dowry gifts double those of the Princess of Yongjia the elder.
translations.idiomatic: As the Princess of Changle was about to marry, the emperor, who especially loved her as the empress's daughter, ordered officials to provide a dowry twice that given the elder Princess of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰；

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated:

sentences.zh: 「昔漢明帝欲封皇子，曰：『我子豈得與先帝子比！

translations.literal: "In former times Emperor Ming of Han wished to enfeoff his princes and said, 'How can my sons be compared with the Former Emperor's sons!
translations.idiomatic: "In former times, when Emperor Ming of Han wished to enfeoff his sons, he said, 'How can my sons be compared with the Former Emperor's sons!

sentences.zh: 』皆令半楚、淮陽。

translations.literal: ' He made them all receive half of Chu and Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: ' He granted them all half the domains of Chu and Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 今資送公主，倍於長主，得無異於明帝之意乎！

translations.literal: Now the dowry for the princess is double that of the elder princess—is this not different from Emperor Ming's intent!
translations.idiomatic: Now the princess's dowry is double the elder princess's—is this not at odds with Emperor Ming's intent!

sentences.zh: 」上然其言，入告皇后。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words and went in to tell the empress.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and went in to tell the empress.

sentences.zh: 後歎曰：「妾亟聞陛下稱重魏徵，不知其故，今觀其引禮義以抑人主之情，乃知真社稷之臣也！

translations.literal: The empress sighed and said, "I have often heard Your Majesty praise Wei Zheng heavily but did not know the reason; now seeing him cite ritual and righteousness to restrain the sovereign's feelings, I know he is truly a minister of the altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: The empress sighed and said, "I have often heard Your Majesty praise Wei Zheng but did not understand why; now, seeing him invoke ritual and righteousness to restrain the sovereign's impulses, I know he is truly a pillar of the state!

sentences.zh: 妾與陛下結髮為夫婦，曲承恩禮，每言必先候顏色，不敢輕犯威嚴；

translations.literal: I bound my hair with Your Majesty to become husband and wife and have bent to receive favor and courtesy; whenever I speak I must first watch Your Majesty's expression and dare not lightly transgress Your Majesty's majesty;
translations.idiomatic: I have been Your Majesty's wife since we bound our hair together and have bent to receive your favor; whenever I speak I must first watch your expression and dare not lightly offend your dignity;

sentences.zh: 況以人臣之疏遠，乃能抗言如是，陛下不可不從也。

translations.literal: how much more when a subject, distant and removed, can speak against you like this—Your Majesty cannot but follow him.
translations.idiomatic: yet a distant subject can speak against you so boldly—Your Majesty cannot but heed him.

sentences.zh: 」因請遣中使繼錢四百緡、絹四百匹以賜征，且語之曰：「聞公正直，乃今見之，故以相賞。

translations.literal: " She then asked that a palace envoy be sent with four hundred strings of cash and four hundred bolts of silk to reward Zheng, and also told him, "I have heard that you are upright; only now do I see it, and therefore reward you.
translations.idiomatic: " She then asked that a palace envoy be sent with four hundred strings of cash and four hundred bolts of silk for Zheng, with this message: "I have heard you are upright; only now do I see it, and therefore reward you.

sentences.zh: 公宜常秉此心，勿轉移也。

translations.literal: You, sir, should always hold this heart and not shift from it.
translations.idiomatic: Hold fast to this heart and do not waver from it.

sentences.zh: 」上嘗罷朝，怒曰：「會須殺此田舍翁。

translations.literal: " The emperor once, after dismissing court, said in anger, "I shall have to kill this rustic old fellow."
translations.idiomatic: " Once after court the emperor said in anger, "I shall have to kill that rustic old fellow."

sentences.zh: 」後問為誰，上曰：「魏徵每廷辱我。

translations.literal: " The empress asked whom he meant; the emperor said, "Wei Zheng insults me in court every day."
translations.idiomatic: " The empress asked whom he meant; the emperor said, "Wei Zheng humiliates me in court every day."

sentences.zh: 」後退，具朝服立於庭，上驚問其故。

translations.literal: " The empress withdrew, put on full court dress, and stood in the courtyard; the emperor was startled and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress withdrew, dressed in full court regalia, and stood in the courtyard; the emperor was startled and asked why.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「妾聞主明臣直；

translations.literal: The empress said, "I have heard that when the ruler is enlightened the minister is upright;
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "I have heard that when the ruler is enlightened the minister is upright;

sentences.zh: 今魏徵直，由陛下之明故也，妾敢不賀！

translations.literal: now Wei Zheng is upright because Your Majesty is enlightened—how dare I not congratulate!
translations.idiomatic: now Wei Zheng is upright because Your Majesty is enlightened—how could I not congratulate you!

sentences.zh: 」上乃悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was then pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛卯，襄州都督鄒襄公張公謹卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinmao Zhang Gongjin, Duke of Zouxiang, regional commander of Xiang Prefecture, died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinmao Zhang Gongjin, Duke of Zouxiang and regional commander of Xiang Prefecture, died.

sentences.zh: 明日，上出次發哀。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor went out to a lodging place to express mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor went out to a temporary lodging to mourn.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，辰日忌哭。

translations.literal: The authorities reported that on a chen day weeping was taboo.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported that weeping was taboo on chen days.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「君之於臣，猶父子也，情發於衷，安避辰日！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Between ruler and minister it is like father and son; when feeling bursts from the heart, how can one avoid a chen day!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Between ruler and minister the bond is like father and son; when grief rises from the heart, how can one heed a chen day!

sentences.zh: 」遂哭之。

translations.literal: " He then wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept for him.

sentences.zh: 六月，己亥，金州刺史酆悼王元亨薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on jihai Prince Yuanheng, Prince Dao of Feng, prefect of Jin, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month on jihai Prince Yuanheng, Prince Dao of Feng and prefect of Jin, died.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，江王囂薨。

translations.literal: On xinhai Prince Xiao of Jiang died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Prince Xiao of Jiang died.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙辰，焉耆王突騎支遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingchen King Tuqizhi of Yanqi sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingchen King Tuqizhi of Yanqi sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 初，焉耆入中國由磧路，隋末閉塞，道由高昌；

translations.literal: Earlier Yanqi's route into China was by the desert road; at the end of Sui it was blocked and the route went through Gaochang;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yanqi had entered China by the desert route; at the end of Sui that road was closed and traffic went through Gaochang;

sentences.zh: 突騎支請復開磧路以便往來，上許之。

translations.literal: Tuqizhi requested that the desert road be reopened to facilitate coming and going; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Tuqizhi asked that the desert route be reopened for easier travel; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 由是高昌恨之，遣兵襲焉耆，大掠而去。

translations.literal: Because of this Gaochang resented it and sent troops to raid Yanqi, plundering greatly before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang resented this and sent troops to raid Yanqi, plundering heavily before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 辛未，宴三品已上於丹霄殿。

translations.literal: On xinwei he feasted officials of the third rank and above in Danxiao Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he feasted officials of the third rank and above in Danxiao Hall.

sentences.zh: 上從容言曰：「中外又安，皆公卿之力。

translations.literal: The emperor said at ease, "Within and without are again at peace—all through the strength of you dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said calmly, "Peace reigns at home and abroad—all through your efforts, dukes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 然隋煬帝威加夷、夏，頡利跨有北荒，統葉護雄據西域，今皆覆亡，此乃朕與公等所親見，勿矜強盛以自滿也！

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Yang of Sui made his might extend over Yi and Xia, Jieli held the northern wastes, and Tong Yehu dominated the Western Regions—now all have perished. This is what I and you, sirs, have seen with our own eyes; do not pride yourselves on strength and grow complacent!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Yang of Sui awed Yi and Xia, Jieli held the northern wastes, and Tong Yehu dominated the Western Regions—all are now gone. This we have seen with our own eyes; do not pride yourselves on strength and grow complacent!

sentences.zh: 西突厥肆葉護可汗發兵擊薛延陀，為薛延陀所敗。

translations.literal: Ashina Helu, qaghan of the Western Turks, sent troops to attack the Xueyantuo and was defeated by the Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Helu, qaghan of the Western Turks, attacked the Xueyantuo and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護性猜狠，信讒；

translations.literal: Ashina Helu was by nature suspicious and cruel and trusted slander;
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Helu was suspicious and cruel and trusted slander;

sentences.zh: 有乙利可汗，功最多，肆葉護以非其族類，誅滅之，由是諸部皆不自保。

translations.literal: there was Yili Qaghan, whose achievements were greatest; Ashina Helu, because he was not of his clan, executed and destroyed him, whereupon all the tribes could no longer protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yili Qaghan had achieved the most, but Ashina Helu, because he was not of his clan, executed him, and thereafter the tribes could no longer trust their safety.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護又忌莫賀設之子泥孰，陰欲圖之，泥孰奔焉耆。

translations.literal: Ashina Helu also envied Nishuo, son of Moheshe, and secretly wished to plot against him; Nishuo fled to Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Helu also envied Nishuo, son of Moheshe, and secretly plotted against him; Nishuo fled to Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 設卑達官與弩失畢二部攻之，肆葉護輕騎奔康居，尋卒。

translations.literal: Shebeidaguan and the two tribes of Nushibi attacked him; Ashina Helu fled lightly mounted to Kangju and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Shebeidaguan and the Nushibi tribes attacked him; Ashina Helu fled lightly mounted to Kangju and soon died.

sentences.zh: 國人迎泥孰於焉耆而立之，是為咄陸可汗，遣使內附。

translations.literal: The people welcomed Nishuo from Yanqi and established him; this was Qulü Qaghan, who sent envoys to submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: The people welcomed Nishuo from Yanqi and enthroned him as Qulü Qaghan, who sent envoys to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，遣鴻臚少卿劉善因立咄陸為奚利邲咄陸可汗。

translations.literal: On dingyou he sent Vice Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Reception Liu Shanyin to install Qulü as Qaghan Qulü of the Xili.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he sent Vice Minister Liu Shanyin of the Court for Diplomatic Reception to install Qulü as Qaghan Qulü of the Xili.

sentences.zh: 閏月，乙卯，上宴近臣於丹霄殿，長孫無忌曰；

translations.literal: In the intercalary month on yimao the emperor feasted close ministers in Danxiao Hall; Zhangsun Wuji said:
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month on yimao the emperor feasted close ministers in Danxiao Hall; Zhangsun Wuji said:

sentences.zh: 「王珪、魏徵，昔為仇讎，不謂今日得同此宴。

translations.literal: "Wang Gui and Wei Zheng were once mortal enemies; I did not expect that today they could share this feast.
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Gui and Wei Zheng were once mortal enemies—I never expected to see them at the same feast today.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「征、珪盡心所事，故我用之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Zheng and Gui devoted their hearts to those they served; therefore I employ them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Zheng and Gui gave their full loyalty to those they served; that is why I employ them.

sentences.zh: 然征每諫，我不從，我與之言輒不應，何也？

translations.literal: Yet whenever Zheng remonstrates and I do not follow, if I speak with him he invariably does not respond—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever Zheng remonstrates and I refuse, if I speak to him afterward he will not answer—why?

sentences.zh: 」魏徵對曰：「臣以事為不可，故諫；

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng replied, "This subject holds the matter impossible and therefore remonstrates;
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng replied, "I remonstrate because I hold the matter wrong;

sentences.zh: 若陛下不從而臣應之，則事遂施行，故不敢應。

translations.literal: if Your Majesty does not follow and this subject responds, then the matter will proceed to implementation; therefore I dare not respond.
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty refuses and I answer you, the matter will proceed as decided; therefore I dare not answer.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「且應而復諫，庸何傷！

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Respond first and remonstrate again—what harm!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Answer first and remonstrate again—what harm is there in that!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「昔舜戒郡臣：『爾無面從，退有後言。

translations.literal: " He replied, "In former times Shun warned the regional ministers: 'Do not agree to my face and speak otherwise behind my back.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Shun once warned his ministers: 'Do not agree to my face and speak otherwise behind my back.

sentences.zh: 』臣心知其非而口應陛下，乃面從也，豈稷、契事舜之意邪！

translations.literal: ' If in my heart I know it is wrong yet with my mouth I assent to Your Majesty, that is agreeing to the face—how would that be the intent of Hou Ji and Qi in serving Shun!
translations.idiomatic: ' If I know in my heart that something is wrong yet assent with my mouth, that is agreeing to your face—is that how Hou Ji and Qi served Shun!

sentences.zh: 」上大笑曰：「人言魏徵舉止疏慢，我視之更覺嫵媚，正為此耳！

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed greatly and said, "People say Wei Zheng's bearing is coarse and slow, but when I look at him I find him all the more charming—just for this!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and said, "People say Wei Zheng is blunt and rough in manner, but I find him all the more winning—just for this!

sentences.zh: 」征起，拜謝曰：「陛下開臣使言，故臣得盡其愚，若陛下拒而不受，臣何敢數犯顏色乎！

translations.literal: " Zheng rose, bowed, and thanked him, saying, "Your Majesty opens this subject so that he may speak; therefore I can exhaust my foolishness. If Your Majesty refused and would not accept, how would I dare repeatedly offend Your Majesty's countenance!
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng rose, bowed, and said, "Your Majesty encourages me to speak, and so I can offer all I have; if Your Majesty refused to listen, how would I dare repeatedly offend you!

sentences.zh: 戊辰，秘書少監虞世南上《聖德論》，上賜手詔，稱：「卿論太高。

translations.literal: On wuchen Yu Shinan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, submitted the "Discourse on Sagely Virtue"; the emperor bestowed a personal edict, saying, "Your discourse is too lofty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Yu Shinan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, submitted the Discourse on Sagely Virtue; the emperor replied in his own hand, "Your discourse sets the bar too high.

sentences.zh: 朕何敢擬上古！

translations.literal: How would I dare compare myself with high antiquity!
translations.idiomatic: How dare I compare myself with high antiquity!

sentences.zh: 但比近世差勝耳。

translations.literal: I am only somewhat better than recent ages, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: I am only somewhat better than recent times, that is all.

sentences.zh: 然卿適睹其始，未知其終。

translations.literal: Yet you have only just seen the beginning and do not know the end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have only seen the beginning and do not know how it will end.

sentences.zh: 若朕能慎終如始，則此論可傳；

translations.literal: If I can be careful at the end as at the beginning, then this discourse may be transmitted;
translations.idiomatic: If I can be as careful at the end as at the beginning, this discourse may endure;

sentences.zh: 如或不然，恐徒使後世笑卿也。

translations.literal: if not, I fear it will only make later ages laugh at you.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise I fear later ages will only laugh at you.

sentences.zh: 九月，己酉，幸慶善宮，上生時故宅也，因與貴臣宴，賦詩。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on jiyou he visited Qingshan Palace, the former house where the emperor was born; there he feasted with honored ministers and composed poetry.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month on jiyou he visited Qingshan Palace, his birthplace, and feasted with honored ministers, composing poetry.

sentences.zh: 起居郎清平呂才被之管弦，命曰：「《功成慶善樂》，使童子八佾為《九功之舞》，大宴會，與《破陳舞》偕奏於庭。

translations.literal: Attendant of the Bedchamber Lü Cai of Qingping set it to strings and pipes and named it "Music of Achievement and Qingshan Celebration," ordering boys in eight rows to perform the "Dance of the Nine Achievements"; at the great feast it was played in the courtyard together with the "Dance of Breaking Chen."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant of the Bedchamber Lü Cai set it to music and named it Music of Achievement and Qingshan Celebration, with boys in eight rows performing the Dance of the Nine Achievements; at the great feast it was played in the courtyard together with the Dance of Breaking Chen.

sentences.zh: 同州刺史尉遲敬德預宴，有班在其上者，敬德怒曰：「汝何功，坐我上！

translations.literal: Yuchi Jingde, prefect of Tong Prefecture, attended the feast; when someone of lower rank sat above him, Jingde said in anger, "What achievement have you, that you sit above me!
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde of Tong Prefecture attended the feast; when a man of lower rank sat above him, Jingde said angrily, "What have you done to sit above me!

sentences.zh: 」任城王道宗次其下，諭解之。

translations.literal: " Prince Daozong of Rencheng sat below him and admonished him to desist.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince Daozong of Rencheng, seated below, tried to calm him.

sentences.zh: 敬德拳毆道宗，目幾眇。

translations.literal: Jingde struck Daozong with his fists and nearly blinded his eye.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde punched Daozong and nearly blinded him in one eye.

sentences.zh: 上不懌而罷，謂敬德曰：「朕見漢高祖誅滅功臣，意常尤之，故欲與卿等共保富貴，令子孫不絕。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and dismissed the feast; he told Jingde, "I have seen how Emperor Gaozu of Han executed and destroyed his meritorious ministers and have always blamed it; therefore I wished to share wealth and honor with you, sirs, so that your descendants would not perish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and ended the feast; he told Jingde, "I have always blamed Gaozu of Han for destroying his meritorious ministers, and wished to share wealth and honor with you so your lines would not end.

sentences.zh: 然卿居官數犯法，乃知韓、彭菹醢，非高祖之罪也。

translations.literal: Yet you, sir, in office repeatedly violate the law—now I know that Han Xin and Peng Yue were minced and pickled, and it was not Gaozu's fault alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you repeatedly break the law in office—now I see that Han Xin and Peng Yue were executed, and Gaozu was not solely to blame.

sentences.zh: 國家綱紀，唯賞與罰，非分之恩，不可數得，勉自修飭，無貽後悔！

translations.literal: The state's discipline rests only on reward and punishment; favors beyond measure cannot be gained repeatedly—strive to restrain yourself and leave no cause for regret!
translations.idiomatic: The state's order rests on reward and punishment alone; undue favor cannot be granted again and again—discipline yourself and leave no cause for regret!

sentences.zh: 」敬德由是始懼而自戢。

translations.literal: " From this Jingde began to fear and restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: " From this Jingde began to fear and restrain himself.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，秦州刺史崔善爲卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: On xinmao Cui Shanwei, prefect of Qin, died at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Cui Shanwei, prefect of Qin, died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙卯，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yimao, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yimao, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝侍上皇宴於大安宮，帝與皇后更獻飲膳及服御之物，夜久乃罷。

translations.literal: The emperor attended the Retired Emperor's feast in Da'an Palace; the emperor and empress in turn presented food, drink, and garments and furnishings; only late at night did it end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended the Retired Emperor's feast in Da'an Palace; he and the empress in turn presented food, drink, and garments; the feast lasted deep into the night.

sentences.zh: 帝親為上皇捧輿至殿門，上皇不許，命太子代之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally bore the Retired Emperor's carriage to the hall gate; the Retired Emperor would not allow it and ordered the crown prince to take his place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally bore the Retired Emperor's carriage to the hall gate; the Retired Emperor refused and had the crown prince take his place.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗鬱鬱不得意，數與家人相對悲泣，容貌羸憊。

translations.literal: Jieli Qaghan of the Turks was depressed and discontented, often weeping in grief with his family face to face; his appearance was wasted and weary.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli Qaghan of the Turks was depressed and discontented, often weeping with his family; he looked wasted and weary.

sentences.zh: 上見而憐之，以虢州地多麋鹿，可以遊獵，乃以頡利為虢州刺史；

translations.literal: The emperor saw this and pitied him; because Guo Prefecture had many elk and deer suitable for hunting, he made Jieli prefect of Guo;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied him and, because Guo Prefecture had many elk for hunting, appointed Jieli its prefect;

sentences.zh: 頡利辭，不願往。

translations.literal: Jieli declined and did not wish to go.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli declined and would not go.

sentences.zh: 癸未，復以為右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On guiwei he was again made Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he was again made Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛巳，契苾酋長何力帥部落六千餘家詣沙州降，詔處之於甘、涼之間，以何力為左領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on xinsi, Qibi chieftain Heli led more than six thousand households of his tribe to surrender at Sha Prefecture; an edict settled them between Gan and Liang, and Heli was made General of the Left Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month on xinsi, Qibi chieftain Heli led more than six thousand households to surrender at Sha Prefecture; they were settled between Gan and Liang, and Heli was made General of the Left Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以左光祿大夫陳叔達為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: On gengyin Chen Shuda, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, was made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Chen Shuda was made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝謂叔達曰：「卿武德中有讜言，故以此官相報。

translations.literal: The emperor told Shuda, "In the Wude reign you spoke forthright words; therefore I repay you with this office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Shuda, "In the Wude reign you spoke forthrightly; I repay you with this office.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣見隋室父子相殘，以取亂亡，當日之言，非為陛下，乃社稷之計耳。

translations.literal: " He replied, "This subject saw the Sui house with father and son harming each other, bringing disorder and ruin; my words that day were not for Your Majesty but for the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I saw the Sui house destroy itself through father and son turning on each other; my words that day were not for you personally but for the state."

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸丑，帝與侍臣論安危之本。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on guichou the emperor discussed with attending ministers the root of security and peril.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month on guichou the emperor discussed with his ministers the foundations of security and peril.

sentences.zh: 中書令溫彥博曰：「伏願陛下常如貞觀初，則善矣。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of the Secretariat Wen Yanbo said, "I humbly wish Your Majesty would always be as at the beginning of Zhenguan—then it would be well.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Wen Yanbo said, "I humbly wish Your Majesty would always be as at the beginning of Zhenguan—that would be best.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕比來怠於為政乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Have I lately been slack in governing?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Have I lately been slack in governing?

sentences.zh: 」魏徵曰：「貞觀之初，陛下志在節儉，求諫不倦。

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng said, "At the beginning of Zhenguan Your Majesty's will was set on frugality and you sought remonstrance without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng said, "At the beginning of Zhenguan Your Majesty was intent on frugality and sought remonstrance tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 比來營繕微多，諫者頗有忤旨，此其所以異耳。

translations.literal: Lately construction and repair have been somewhat more, and remonstrators have often offended Your Majesty's intent—this is where they differ.
translations.idiomatic: Lately construction has increased somewhat, and remonstrators have often met with displeasure—that is the difference.

sentences.zh: 」帝拊掌大笑曰：「誠有是事！

translations.literal: " The emperor clapped his hands and laughed greatly, saying, "It is truly so!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor clapped his hands and laughed, "It is truly so!

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝親錄系囚，見應死者，閔之，縱使歸家，期以來秋來就死。

translations.literal: On xinwei the emperor personally recorded imprisoned convicts; seeing those who should die, he pitied them and released them to return home, fixing the coming autumn for them to come and accept death.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the emperor personally reviewed prisoners; seeing those condemned to death, he pitied them and sent them home, fixing the coming autumn for their return to face execution.

sentences.zh: 仍敕天下死囚，皆縱遣，使至期來詣京師。

translations.literal: He also ordered that death-row prisoners throughout the realm be released and sent away, to come to the capital when the term arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered all death-row prisoners in the realm released to return home and come to the capital when the term arrived.

sentences.zh: 是歲，党項等羌前後內屬者三十萬口。

translations.literal: This year the Qiang of the Dangxiang and others who submitted inwardly before and after numbered three hundred thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: This year three hundred thousand persons of the Dangxiang Qiang and others submitted to the court.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下請封禪者首尾相屬，上諭以「舊有氣疾，恐登高增劇，公等勿復言。

translations.literal: From dukes and ministers downward those requesting Feng and Shan followed one after another; the emperor instructed them, "I have long had a qi disorder and fear that climbing high would worsen it—you, sirs, speak no more of it.
translations.idiomatic: Officials requesting Feng and Shan came one after another; the emperor told them, "I have long had a respiratory ailment and fear climbing high would worsen it—speak no more of it.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「朕比來決事或不能皆如律令，公輩以為事小，不復執奏。

translations.literal: The emperor told attending ministers, "Lately in deciding affairs I sometimes cannot entirely follow statutes and ordinances; you, sirs, think the matter small and no longer memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "Lately when I decide affairs I sometimes deviate from law; you treat such matters as small and no longer memorialize.

sentences.zh: 夫事無不由小以致大，此乃危亡之端也。

translations.literal: Affairs are never without proceeding from small to great—this is the beginning of peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing grows large except from small beginnings—this is how states fall.

sentences.zh: 昔關龍逄忠諫而死，朕每痛之。

translations.literal: In former times Guan Longfeng died for loyal remonstrance; I grieve for it each time.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Longfeng died for loyal remonstrance—I grieve for it each time I think of it.

sentences.zh: 煬帝驕暴而亡，公輩所親見也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang perished through arrogance and cruelty—you, sirs, saw it with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang perished through arrogance and cruelty—you saw it yourselves.

sentences.zh: 公輩常宜為朕思煬帝之亡，朕常為公輩念關龍逄之死，何患君臣不相保乎！

translations.literal: You, sirs, should often think for me of Emperor Yang's ruin; I often think for you, sirs, of Guan Longfeng's death—what worry is there that ruler and minister cannot protect each other!
translations.idiomatic: You should often think of Emperor Yang's fall for my sake; I often think of Guan Longfeng's death for yours—why should ruler and minister fail to protect each other!

sentences.zh: 上謂魏徵曰：「為官擇人，不可造次。

translations.literal: The emperor told Wei Zheng, "In appointing officials one chooses men—this cannot be done hastily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Wei Zheng, "In appointing officials one must choose men carefully—this cannot be rushed.

sentences.zh: 用一君子，則君子皆至；

translations.literal: Employ one gentleman and gentlemen all come;
translations.idiomatic: Employ one gentleman and gentlemen will all come;

sentences.zh: 用一小人，則小人競進矣。

translations.literal: employ one petty man and petty men vie to advance.
translations.idiomatic: employ one petty man and petty men will vie to advance.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「然。

translations.literal: " He replied, "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "That is so.

sentences.zh: 天下未定，則專取其才，不考其行；

translations.literal: When the realm is not settled, then take only talent and do not examine conduct;
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is unsettled, take talent alone and do not examine conduct;

sentences.zh: 喪亂既平，則非才行兼備不可用也。

translations.literal: once disorder is pacified, then unless talent and conduct are both complete one cannot be employed.
translations.idiomatic: once order is restored, only those with both talent and conduct may be employed.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，更名《破陳樂》曰《七德舞》。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the "Music of Breaking Chen" was renamed the "Dance of the Seven Virtues."
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Music of Breaking Chen was renamed the Dance of the Seven Virtues.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，宴三品已上及州牧、蠻夷酋長於玄武門，奏《七德》、《九功》之舞。

translations.literal: On guisi he feasted officials of the third rank and above, prefectural governors, and chieftains of barbarians at Xuanwu Gate, performing the dances of the Seven Virtues and Nine Achievements.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he feasted officials of the third rank and above, prefectural governors, and barbarian chieftains at Xuanwu Gate, with performances of the Seven Virtues and Nine Achievements.

sentences.zh: 太常卿蕭瑀上言：「《七德舞》形容聖功，有所未盡，請寫劉武周、薛仁果、竇建德、王世充等擒獲之狀。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xiao Yu submitted, saying, "The Dance of the Seven Virtues depicts sagely achievement but does not exhaust it; I request that scenes of capturing Liu Wuzhou, Xue Renguo, Dou Jiande, Wang Shichong, and others be painted.
translations.idiomatic: Director Xiao Yu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted that the Dance of the Seven Virtues did not fully depict sagely achievement and asked that scenes of capturing Liu Wuzhou, Xue Renguo, Dou Jiande, Wang Shichong, and others be added.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「彼皆一時英雄，今朝廷之臣往往嘗北面事之，若睹其故主屈辱之狀，能不傷其心乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "They were all heroes of their time; many ministers at court today once served them facing north—if they saw their former lords in humiliated states, could their hearts not be wounded?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "They were heroes of their day; many present ministers once served them—if they saw their former lords humiliated, would their hearts not be wounded?

sentences.zh: 」瑀謝曰：「此非臣愚慮所及。

translations.literal: " Yu apologized, saying, "This was not within this subject's foolish consideration.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu apologized, "I did not think of that.

sentences.zh: 」魏徵欲上偃武修文，每侍宴，見《七德舞》輒俯首不視，見《九功舞》則諦觀之。

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng wished to lead the emperor to cease arms and cultivate culture; whenever he attended a feast, seeing the Dance of the Seven Virtues he would bow his head and not look, but seeing the Dance of Nine Achievements he would gaze attentively.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng wished to lead the emperor toward peace and culture; at feasts, when the Seven Virtues was performed he bowed his head and would not look, but when the Nine Achievements was performed he watched attentively.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊子，侍中王珪坐漏洩禁中語，左遷同州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month on wuzi, Wang Gui, Palace Attendant, was demoted for leaking forbidden-palace speech and transferred to be prefect of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month on wuzi, Palace Attendant Wang Gui was demoted for leaking palace secrets and made prefect of Tong.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以秘書監魏徵為侍中。

translations.literal: On gengyin Wei Zheng, Director of the Secretariat, was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Wei Zheng was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 直太史雍人李淳風奏靈台候儀制度疏略，但有赤道，請更造渾天黃道儀，許之。

translations.literal: Direct Astronomer Li Chunfeng of Yong submitted that the observatory instruments' system was coarse and brief, having only the equator; he requested that a armillary sphere with the yellow path be newly made, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Astronomer Li Chunfeng submitted that the observatory instruments were crude, having only the equator, and asked to build a new armillary sphere with the ecliptic; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，成而奏之。

translations.literal: On guisi it was completed and presented.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi it was completed and presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，癸未，上幸九成宮。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on guiwei, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on guiwei, the emperor went to Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 雅州道行軍總管張士貴擊反獠，破之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shigui, campaign commander of the Yazhou circuit, attacked rebellious Liao and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shigui, campaign commander of the Yazhou circuit, attacked rebellious Liao and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙丑，左屯衛大將軍譙敬公周范卒。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on yichou, Zhou Fan, Duke of Qiaojing, Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on yichou, Zhou Fan, Duke of Qiaojing and Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard, died.

sentences.zh: 上行幸，常令范與房玄齡居守。

translations.literal: When the emperor traveled in favor he often ordered Fan and Fang Xuanling to remain and guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled he often left Fan and Fang Xuanling to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 范為人忠篤嚴正，疾甚，不肯出外，竟終於內省，與玄齡相抱而訣曰：「所恨不獲再奉聖顏！

translations.literal: Fan was by nature loyal, sincere, stern, and upright; when his illness was severe he would not go outside and finally died in the inner secretariat; embracing Xuanling in farewell he said, "My regret is that I cannot again behold the sage countenance!
translations.idiomatic: Fan was loyal, sincere, and upright; when gravely ill he would not leave the palace and died in the inner secretariat; embracing Xuanling he said, "I regret that I cannot again behold the sage countenance!

sentences.zh: 辛未，以張士貴為龔州道行軍總管，使擊反獠。

translations.literal: On xinwei Zhang Shigui was made campaign commander of the Gongzhou circuit to attack rebellious Liao.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Zhang Shigui was made campaign commander of the Gongzhou circuit to attack rebellious Liao.

sentences.zh: 九月，山東、河南四十餘州水，遣使賑之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month more than forty prefectures in Shandong and Henan suffered floods; envoys were sent to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month floods struck more than forty prefectures in Shandong and Henan; envoys were sent with relief.

sentences.zh: 去歲所縱天下死囚凡三百九十人，無人督帥，皆如期自詣朝堂，無一人亡匿者；

translations.literal: Of the death-row prisoners released throughout the realm last year, three hundred ninety in all, with no one to supervise or lead them, all came to court on schedule by themselves, and not one fled or hid;
translations.idiomatic: Of the three hundred ninety death-row prisoners released last year, with no escort, all came to court on schedule, and not one fled;

sentences.zh: 上皆赦之。

translations.literal: the emperor pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚申，上還京師。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, the emperor returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬辰，以開府儀同三司長孫無忌為司空，無忌固辭曰：「臣忝預外戚，恐天下謂陛下為私。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on renchen Zhangsun Wuji, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Opening of a Government Office, was made Minister of Works; Wuji firmly declined, saying, "This subject undeservedly shares in the empress's kin and fears the realm will say Your Majesty acts from private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month on renchen Zhangsun Wuji was made Minister of Works; Wuji firmly declined, saying, "I am undeservedly of the empress's kin and fear the realm will say Your Majesty acts from favoritism.

sentences.zh: 」上不許，曰：「吾為官擇人，惟才是與。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not allow it and said, "I choose men for office and give only to those with talent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused and said, "I choose men for office by talent alone.

sentences.zh: 苟或不才，雖親不用，襄邑王神符是也；

translations.literal: If without talent, though kin I do not employ—Prince Shenfu of Xiangyi is such a case;
translations.idiomatic: If without talent, though kin I will not employ—Prince Shenfu of Xiangyi is such a case;

sentences.zh: 如其有才，雖仇不充，魏徵等是也。

translations.literal: if with talent, though an enemy I do not pass over—Wei Zheng and others are such cases.
translations.idiomatic: if with talent, though an enemy I will not pass over—Wei Zheng and others are such cases.

sentences.zh: 今日之舉，非私親也。

translations.literal: Today's appointment is not from private kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Today's appointment is not from private kinship.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲寅，上幸芙蓉園；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on jiayin the emperor visited Furong Garden;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month on jiayin the emperor visited Furong Garden;

sentences.zh: 丙辰，校獵少陵原。

translations.literal: on bingchen he conducted a hunt review on Shaoling Plain.
translations.idiomatic: on bingchen he hunted on Shaoling Plain.

sentences.zh: 戊午，還宮，從上皇置酒故漢未央宮。

translations.literal: On wuwu he returned to the palace and followed the Retired Emperor in setting wine at the former Han Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu he returned to the palace and, with the Retired Emperor, set wine at the former Han Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 上皇命突厥頡利可汗起舞，又命南蠻酋長馮智戴詠詩，既而笑曰：「胡、越一家，自古未有也！

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor ordered Jieli Qaghan of the Turks to dance and also ordered the southern barbarian chieftain Feng Zhidai to recite poetry; then he laughed and said, "Hu and Yue as one family—never since antiquity!
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor had Jieli Qaghan of the Turks dance and the southern chieftain Feng Zhidai recite poetry; then he laughed and said, "Hu and Yue as one family—never since antiquity!

sentences.zh: 」帝奉觴上壽曰：「今四夷入臣，皆陛下教誨，非臣智力所及。

translations.literal: " The emperor raised his cup and offered longevity, saying, "Now the four barbarians enter as subjects—all through Your Majesty's teaching and guidance, not what this subject's intelligence could reach.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor raised his cup and offered longevity, saying, "Now the four quarters submit—all through Your Majesty's teaching, not my own ability.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖亦從太上皇置酒此宮，妄自矜大，臣所不取也。

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Gaozu of Han also followed the Supreme Emperor in setting wine in this palace and vaunted himself arrogantly—what this subject will not take.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Han also feasted the Supreme Emperor here and vaunted himself arrogantly—that I will not do.

sentences.zh: 」上皇大悅。

translations.literal: " The Retired Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The Retired Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 殿上皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: All in the hall shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: All in the hall shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 帝謂左庶子於志寧、右庶子杜正倫曰：「朕年十八，猶在民間，民之疾苦情偽，無不知之。

translations.literal: The emperor told Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent Yu Zhining and Right Guardian Du Zhenglun, "When I was eighteen I was still among the people; the people's suffering and hardship, truth and falsehood—I knew them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Left Guardian Yu Zhining and Right Guardian Du Zhenglun, "At eighteen I was still among the people and knew all their hardships and deceptions.

sentences.zh: 及居大位，區處世務，猶有差失。

translations.literal: When I came to the great position and disposed worldly affairs, there were still errors.
translations.idiomatic: Even after taking the throne and handling affairs of state, I still make mistakes.

sentences.zh: 況太子生長深宮，百姓艱難，耳目所未涉，能無驕逸乎？

translations.literal: How much more the crown prince, reared in the deep palace—what the people's hardship is his eyes and ears have never touched; how can he be without arrogance and dissipation?
translations.idiomatic: How much more the crown prince, reared deep in the palace, who has never seen the people's hardship—how can he avoid arrogance and dissipation?

sentences.zh: 卿等不可不極諫。

translations.literal: You, sirs, cannot but remonstrate to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: You must remonstrate with him to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 」太子好嬉戲，頗虧禮法，志寧與右庶子孔穎達數直諫，上聞而嘉之，各賜金一斤，帛五百匹。

translations.literal: " The crown prince loved play and games and somewhat lacked ritual and law; Zhining and Right Guardian Kong Yingda several times remonstrated directly; when the emperor heard he commended them and gave each a catty of gold and five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince loved play and often neglected ritual propriety; Zhining and Right Guardian Kong Yingda remonstrated repeatedly; the emperor commended them and gave each a catty of gold and five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書段綸奏征巧工楊思齊，上令試之。

translations.literal: Duan Lun, Minister of Works, memorialized to summon the skilled artisan Yang Siqi; the emperor ordered him tested.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Duan Lun memorialized to summon the skilled artisan Yang Siqi; the emperor ordered a test.

sentences.zh: 綸使先造傀儡。

translations.literal: Lun had him first make puppets.
translations.idiomatic: Lun had him first make puppets.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「得巧工庶供國事，卿令先造戲具，豈百工相戒無作淫巧之意邪！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Having a skilled artisan might supply state affairs—yet you, sir, had him first make playthings; is this not contrary to the hundred crafts' mutual admonition not to make licentious cleverness!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A skilled artisan should serve state affairs—yet you had him make toys first; is that not contrary to the crafts' rule against frivolous ingenuity!

sentences.zh: 」乃削綸階。

translations.literal: " He then reduced Lun's rank.
translations.idiomatic: " He then reduced Lun's rank.

sentences.zh: 嘉、陵州獠反，命邗江府統軍牛進達擊破之。

translations.literal: The Liao of Jia and Ling prefectures rebelled; he ordered Niu Jinda, commander-in-chief of Hanjiang Prefecture, to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao of Jia and Ling prefectures rebelled; Niu Jinda, commander of Hanjiang Prefecture, was ordered to attack and defeat them.

sentences.zh: 上問魏徵曰：「群臣上書可采，及召對多失次，何也？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Wei Zheng, "When ministers submit memorials they are often worth adopting, yet when summoned to answer many lose their order—why?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Wei Zheng, "Ministers' memorials are often sound, yet when summoned to court many lose their composure—why?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣觀百司奏事，常數日思之，及至上前，三分不能道一。

translations.literal: " He replied, "This subject observes that when the hundred offices report affairs they often ponder for several days, yet when they reach before Your Majesty they cannot speak one part in three.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I observe that officials often ponder their reports for days, yet before Your Majesty they can scarcely say a third of what they prepared.

sentences.zh: 況諫者拂意觸忌，非陛下借之辭色，豈敢盡其情哉！

translations.literal: How much more when remonstrators go against intent and touch taboos—unless Your Majesty lends them a favorable countenance, how would they dare exhaust their feelings!
translations.idiomatic: How much more remonstrators, who go against your intent and touch taboos—unless Your Majesty lends them a favorable countenance, how would they dare speak their full mind!

sentences.zh: 」上由是接群臣辭色愈溫，嘗曰：「煬帝多猜忌，臨朝對群臣多不語。

translations.literal: " From this the emperor received ministers with ever warmer expression and once said, "Emperor Yang was much given to suspicion; at court facing ministers he often did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " From this the emperor received ministers with ever warmer expression and once said, "Emperor Yang was suspicious; at court he often would not speak to his ministers.

sentences.zh: 朕則不然，與群臣相親如一體耳。

translations.literal: I am not so—I am intimate with ministers as one body.
translations.idiomatic: I am not so—I am intimate with my ministers as one body.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸未，突厥頡利可汗卒。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guiwei, the Türk qaghan Jiali died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guiwei, the Türk qaghan Jiali died.

sentences.zh: 命國人從其俗，焚屍葬之。

translations.literal: He ordered his people to follow their custom and bury him by cremation.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered his people to observe their custom and bury him by cremating the body.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，行軍總管張士貴討東、西王洞反獠，平之。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Mobile Campaign Commander Zhang Shigui campaigned against the rebellious Liao of the Eastern and Western King Caves and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Mobile Campaign Commander Zhang Shigui marched against the rebell Liao of the Eastern and Western King Caves and put them down.

sentences.zh: 上欲分遣大臣為諸道黜陟大使，未得其人；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to dispatch great ministers as investigation-and-promotion envoys for the various circuits but had not found suitable men;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to send senior ministers out as circuit envoys to investigate and promote or demote local officials, but had not yet found the right men;

sentences.zh: 李靖薦魏徵。

translations.literal: Li Jing recommended Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing recommended Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「征箴規朕失，不可一日離左右。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Zheng admonishes and corrects my faults—I cannot have him away from my side even for a day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zheng counsels me on my faults; I cannot have him away from my side even for a day.

sentences.zh: 」乃命靖與太常卿蕭瑀等凡十三人分行天下，「察長吏賢不肖，問民間疾苦，禮高年，賑窮乏，起滯淹，俾使者所至，如朕親睹。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered Li Jing, Minister of Ceremonies Xiao Yu, and twelve others in all to tour the realm in separate directions: "Observe whether senior officials are worthy or unworthy, inquire into the people's hardships, honor the aged, relieve the destitute, raise up the overlooked and stagnant—so that wherever the envoys go it shall be as if I witnessed it myself.
translations.idiomatic: " He then appointed Li Jing, Minister of Ceremonies Xiao Yu, and eleven others—thirteen in all—to fan out across the empire with orders to "assess local magistrates for merit or failure, inquire into popular suffering, honor the elderly, aid the destitute, and lift up the overlooked and stagnant, so that wherever the envoys traveled it would be as if the emperor saw with his own eyes.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚辰，上幸九成宮。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengchen, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengchen, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，辛未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the first day of the xinwei cycle, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on the new moon of xinwei, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 初，吐谷渾可汗伏允遣使入貢，未返，大掠鄯州而去。

translations.literal: Initially, the Tuyuhun qaghan Fuyun sent envoys to pay tribute; before they returned, he raided Shazhou on a large scale and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Tuyuhun qaghan Fuyun had sent tribute envoys to court; before they returned, he launched a major raid on Shazhou and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上遣使讓之，征伏允入朝，稱疾不至，仍為其子尊王求婚；

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to rebuke him and summoned Fuyun to court; Fuyun claimed illness and did not come, yet still sought a marriage alliance for his son the Prince of Respect;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to rebuke him and summoned Fuyun to court; Fuyun pleaded illness and stayed away, yet still asked that his son, the Prince of Respect, be allowed to marry into the imperial line;

sentences.zh: 上許之，令其親迎，尊王又不至，乃絕婚，伏允復遣兵寇蘭、廓二州。

translations.literal: The emperor consented and ordered that he come in person to fetch the bride; the Prince of Respect again did not come, so the marriage was broken off, and Fuyun again sent troops to raid Lan and Kuo Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and required the prince to come in person to fetch the bride; when the Prince of Respect again failed to appear, the marriage was called off, and Fuyun sent troops to raid Lan and Kuo Prefectures once more.

sentences.zh: 伏允年老，信其臣天柱王之謀，數犯邊；

translations.literal: Fuyun was old and trusted the schemes of his minister the King of the Pillar of Heaven; he repeatedly violated the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun was aging and trusted the counsel of his minister the King of the Pillar of Heaven; again and again he struck the borders;

sentences.zh: 又執唐使者趙德楷，上遣使諭之，十返；

translations.literal: He also seized the Tang envoy Zhao Dekai; the emperor sent envoys to instruct him, ten times going back and forth;
translations.idiomatic: He also seized the Tang envoy Zhao Dekai; the emperor sent envoys to reason with him, ten round trips in all;

sentences.zh: 又引其使者，臨軒親諭以禍福，伏允終無悛心。

translations.literal: He also had Fuyun's envoys brought before the throne and personally explained fortune and disaster to them, yet Fuyun in the end had no mind to repent.
translations.idiomatic: He even had Fuyun's envoys brought to the throne and personally lectured them on the rewards of submission and the cost of defiance, yet Fuyun never showed the least sign of repentance.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣左驍衛大將軍段志玄為西海道行軍總管，左驍衛將軍樊興為赤水道行軍總管，將邊兵及契苾、党項之眾以擊之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he dispatched Left Mobile Guard General Duan Zhixuan as West Sea Circuit mobile campaign commander and Left Mobile Guard General Fan Xing as Red Water Circuit mobile campaign commander, leading frontier troops and the forces of the Qibi and Tangut to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he appointed Left Mobile Guard General Duan Zhixuan commander of the West Sea route army and Left Mobile Guard General Fan Xing commander of the Red Water route army, leading frontier troops plus Qibi and Tangut auxiliaries against the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，山東、河南、淮、海之間大水。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, great floods struck between Shandong, Henan, the Huai, and the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, great floods ravaged the region between Shandong, Henan, the Huai River, and the sea.

sentences.zh: 上屢請上皇避暑九成宮，上皇以隋文帝終於彼，惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly invited the Retired Emperor to escape the heat at Jiucheng Palace; the Retired Emperor hated the place because Emperor Wen of Sui had died there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly urged the Retired Emperor to spend the summer at Jiucheng Palace, but the Retired Emperor loathed the place because Emperor Wen of Sui had died there.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，營大明宮，以為上皇清暑之所。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, he built Daming Palace to serve as the Retired Emperor's summer retreat.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, he ordered Daming Palace built as a cool retreat for the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 未成而上皇寢疾，不果居。

translations.literal: Before it was finished the Retired Emperor took to his bed with illness and never came to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Before construction was finished the Retired Emperor fell ill and never took up residence there.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，段志玄擊吐谷渾，破之，追奔八百餘里，去青海三十餘里，吐谷渾驅牧馬而遁。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Duan Zhixuan struck the Tuyuhun and defeated them, pursuing the fleeing enemy more than eight hundred li, coming within thirty-odd li of Qinghai; the Tuyuhun drove off their herds and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Duan Zhixuan defeated the Tuyuhun in battle and chased them more than eight hundred li, coming to within thirty-odd li of Qinghai Lake before the Tuyuhun drove off their herds and fled.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上還京師。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the emperor returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 右僕射李靖以疾遜位，許之。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Li Jing resigned on grounds of illness, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Li Jing asked to step down on account of illness, and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛未，以靖為特進，封爵如故，祿賜、吏卒並依舊給，俟疾小瘳，每三兩日至門下、中書平章政事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinwei, Li Jing was made Special Advancement with rank and fief unchanged; salary, gifts, clerks, and attendants were all provided as before; when his illness eased somewhat he was to attend every two or three days at the Secretariat and Chancellery to discuss state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinwei, Li Jing was made Special Advancement, keeping his rank and fief; salaries, gifts, clerks, and attendants continued as before, and whenever his illness eased he was to come every few days to the Secretariat and Chancellery to deliberate on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 甲申，吐蕃贊普棄宗弄贊遣使入貢，仍請婚。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the Tibetan tsenpo Songtsen Gampo sent envoys to pay tribute and also requested a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the Tibetan ruler Songtsen Gampo sent tribute envoys and also sought a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃在吐谷渾西南，近世浸強，蠶食它國，土宇廣大，勝兵數十萬，然未嘗通中國。

translations.literal: Tibet lay southwest of Tuyuhun; in recent generations it had grown gradually stronger, nibbling away at other states; its territory was vast and its effective troops numbered in the hundreds of thousands, yet it had never had contact with the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet lay southwest of Tuyuhun; in recent times it had grown steadily stronger, nibbling at neighboring states until its domain was vast and it could field hundreds of thousands of warriors—yet it had never had formal contact with the Central Realm.

sentences.zh: 其王稱讚普，俗不言姓，王族皆曰論，宦族皆曰尚。

translations.literal: Its king was called tsenpo; by custom surnames were not spoken; all of the royal clan were styled Lun, all of the ministerial clan Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Its king was styled tsenpo; by custom no surname was used—the royal clan took the name Lun, the ministerial clan Shang.

sentences.zh: 棄宗弄贊有勇略，四鄰畏之。

translations.literal: Songtsen Gampo had courage and stratagem; the neighbors on all sides feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Songtsen Gampo was bold and resourceful, and neighboring peoples feared him.

sentences.zh: 上遣使者馮德遐往慰撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the envoy Feng Dexia to go comfort and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the envoy Feng Dexia to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，吐谷渾寇涼州。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Tuyuhun raided Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the Tuyuhun raided Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己丑，下詔大舉討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: On jichou, an edict was issued for a major campaign against the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, an edict was issued ordering a major campaign against the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 上欲得李靖為將，為其老，重勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to have Li Jing as commander but, because he was old, hesitated to impose heavy labor on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted Li Jing to command the campaign but hesitated to burden him, given his age.

sentences.zh: 靖聞之，請行；

translations.literal: When Li Jing heard of this he requested to go;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing heard this, he volunteered to take the field;

sentences.zh: 上大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛丑，以靖為西海道行軍大總管，節度諸軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinchou, Li Jing was made Grand Mobile Campaign Commander of the West Sea Circuit with authority over all armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinchou, Li Jing was appointed Grand Commander of the West Sea route army with authority over all forces.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書侯君集為積石道、刑部尚書任城王道宗為鄯善道、涼州都督李大亮為且末道、岷州都督李道彥為赤水道、利州刺史高甑生為鹽澤道行軍總管，並突厥、契苾之眾擊吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Minister of War Hou Junji was made Jishi Circuit commander, Minister of Justice the Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong Shanshan Circuit commander, Liang Prefecture Military Governor Li Daliang Qiemo Circuit commander, Min Prefecture Military Governor Li Daoyan Red Water Circuit commander, and Li Prefecture Inspector Gao Zengsheng Salt Marsh Circuit mobile campaign commander, all together with Türk and Qibi forces to strike the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Hou Junji was placed in command on the Jishi route, Minister of Justice the Prince of Rencheng on the Shanshan route, Liang Prefecture Military Governor Li Daliang on the Qiemo route, Min Prefecture Military Governor Li Daoyan on the Red Water route, and Li Prefecture Inspector Gao Zengsheng on the Salt Marsh route—each leading Türk and Qibi auxiliaries against the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 帝聘隋通事舍人鄭仁基女為充華，詔已行，冊使將發，魏徵聞其嘗許嫁士人陸爽，遽上表諫。

translations.literal: The emperor betrothed the daughter of Sui Palace Secretariat Attendant Zheng Renji as Lady Who Fills the Court; the edict had already been issued and the investiture envoy was about to depart when Wei Zheng heard she had once been promised in marriage to the scholar Lu Shuang and urgently submitted a remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had chosen the daughter of former Sui official Zheng Renji to enter the inner palace as a consort; the edict was already out and the investiture envoy was about to depart when Wei Zheng learned she had once been pledged to the scholar Lu Shuang and rushed in a memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，大驚，手詔深自克責，命停冊使。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he was greatly alarmed, issued a personal edict deeply blaming himself, and ordered the investiture envoy halted.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he was deeply shaken, wrote a personal edict blaming himself in the strongest terms, and ordered the investiture mission stopped.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡等奏稱：「許嫁陸氏，無顯狀，大禮既行，不可中止。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and others submitted, saying, "The promise of marriage to the Lu clan has no clear evidence; the great rite has already been set in motion and cannot be halted midway.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and others memorialized that there was no clear proof of a promise to the Lu family, that the great rite was already in motion, and that it could not be stopped midway.

sentences.zh: 」爽亦表言初無婚姻之議。

translations.literal: " Lu Shuang also submitted a memorial saying there had never been any talk of marriage at the outset.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Shuang also submitted a memorial denying any prior agreement of marriage.

sentences.zh: 帝謂征曰：「群臣或容希合；

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zheng, "Some among the ministers perhaps merely wish to flatter me;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Wei Zheng, "Some of my ministers are perhaps only telling me what I want to hear;

sentences.zh: 爽亦自陳，何也？

translations.literal: Lu Shuang too speaks for himself—why?
translations.idiomatic: and Lu Shuang has spoken for himself as well—why?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「彼以陛下為外雖捨之，或陰加罪譴，故不得不然。

translations.literal: " He replied, "They suppose that though Your Majesty outwardly releases the matter, you may secretly impose guilt and punishment—so they cannot do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "They fear that although Your Majesty publicly releases the matter, you may secretly punish them—so they have no choice.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「外人意或當如是。

translations.literal: " The emperor smiled and said, "Outsiders' minds perhaps ought to be so.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor smiled and said, "Perhaps ordinary people can be expected to think that way.

sentences.zh: 朕之言未能使人必信如此邪？

translations.literal: Have my words been unable to compel such full trust?
translations.idiomatic: Have my words really failed to inspire that kind of trust?

sentences.zh: 中牟丞皇甫德參上言：「修洛陽宮，勞人；

translations.literal: Zhongmou Assistant Magistrate Huangfu Decan submitted, saying, "Repairing Luoyang Palace burdens the people;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmou Assistant Magistrate Huangfu Decan submitted a memorial saying that repairing Luoyang Palace overworked the people;

sentences.zh: 收地租，厚斂；

translations.literal: collecting land rent is heavy exaction;
translations.idiomatic: that collecting land rent amounted to heavy exaction;

sentences.zh: 俗好高髻，蓋宮中所化。

translations.literal: the custom of wearing high coiffures is probably influenced by the palace.
translations.idiomatic: and that the fashion for high coiffures was probably spread by the palace.

sentences.zh: 」上怒，謂房玄齡等曰：「德參欲國家不役一人，不收斗租，宮人皆無發，乃可其意邪！

translations.literal: " The emperor grew angry and said to Fang Xuanling and the others, "Does Decan want the state to conscript no one, collect no peck of rent, and have palace women all without hair before he will be satisfied!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor grew angry and said to Fang Xuanling and the others, "So Decan would have the state employ no one, collect no grain rent, and have every palace woman go bald before he would be satisfied!

sentences.zh: 」欲治其謗訕之罪。

translations.literal: " He wished to punish him for slander.
translations.idiomatic: " He wanted to punish Decan for defamation.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「賈誼當漢文帝時上書，云『可為痛哭者一，可為流涕者二。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying, "When Jia Yi memorialized under Emperor Wen of Han he wrote, 'There is one thing to weep bitter tears for, two things to shed tears for.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "When Jia Yi memorialized under Emperor Wen of Han he wrote, 'There is one thing worth weeping blood over, two things worth shedding tears over.'

sentences.zh: 』自古上書不激切，不能動人主之心，所謂狂夫之言，聖人擇焉，唯陛下裁察。

translations.literal: ' From antiquity memorials that were not sharp and piercing could not move a ruler's heart; as they say, 'The madman's words—the sage chooses from them.' I beg Your Majesty to judge.
translations.idiomatic: ' From antiquity, memorials that were not sharp could not move a ruler's heart—as the saying goes, 'Even a madman's words may hold something the sage can use.' I beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕罪斯人，則誰復敢言？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "If I punish this man, who will dare speak again?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "If I punish this man, who will dare speak plainly again?

sentences.zh: 」乃賜絹二十匹。

translations.literal: " He thereupon bestowed twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " He then awarded Decan twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 他日，征奏言：「陛下近日不好直言，雖勉強含容，非曩時之豁如。

translations.literal: On another day Zheng submitted, saying, "Your Majesty of late does not welcome blunt speech; though you force yourself to forbear, it is not the openness of former days.
translations.idiomatic: On another day Wei Zheng submitted that the emperor had lately been less receptive to blunt counsel—though he forced himself to be tolerant, he was no longer as open as before.

sentences.zh: 」上乃更加優賜，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: " The emperor then granted additional rewards and appointed him Censor.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then added further rewards and appointed Decan a censor.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人高季輔上言：「外官卑品，猶未得祿，饑寒切身，難保清白，今倉廩浸實，宜量加優給，然後可責以不貪，嚴設科禁。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafting Officer Gao Jifu submitted, saying, "Low-ranking local officials still do not receive salaries; hunger and cold press upon them and it is hard to keep them honest. Now the granaries are gradually full—it is fitting to give them measured extra support; only then can one demand that they not be greedy and strictly set statutes forbidding corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafting Officer Gao Jifu submitted that low-ranking local officials still received no salary, that hunger and cold made honesty hard to sustain, and that now the granaries were filling—it was time to improve their pay so that only then could the court demand integrity and enforce strict anti-corruption laws.

sentences.zh: 又，密王元曉等皆陛下之弟，比見帝子拜諸叔，叔皆答拜，紊亂昭穆，宜訓之以禮。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Prince of Mi Yuan Xiao and the others are all Your Majesty's younger brothers; lately I have seen the emperor's sons bow to their uncles and the uncles return the bow—this confuses senior and junior in the clan rites. They should be instructed in proper ritual.
