translations.idiomatic: He also noted that the Prince of Mi, Yuan Xiao, and the emperor's other brothers were being bowed to by the crown prince's sons, and bowing in return—confusing proper order in the clan rites—and urged that they be taught correct ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，上善之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted the emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 西突厥咄陸可汗卒，其弟同娥設立，是為沙缽羅咥利失可汗。

translations.literal: The Western Türk qaghan Tutun died; his younger brother Tong'e She succeeded him—this was Qaghan Shiboluo Dilishi.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Türk qaghan Tutun died; his younger brother Tong'e She succeeded him as qaghan, taking the title Shiboluo Dilishi.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，党項先內屬者皆叛歸吐谷渾。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Tangut groups formerly under inner allegiance all rebelled and returned to the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Tangut groups that had previously submitted to Tang all rebelled and rejoined the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚辰，洮州羌叛入吐谷渾，殺刺史孔長秀。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengchen, the Qiang of Tao Prefecture rebelled, entered Tuyuhun territory, and killed Prefecture Inspector Kong Changxiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengchen, the Qiang of Tao Prefecture rebelled, crossed into Tuyuhun territory, and killed Prefecture Inspector Kong Changxiu.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，赦天下。

translations.literal: On renchen, a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, the emperor declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，鹽澤道行軍總管高甑生擊叛羌，破之。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Salt Marsh Circuit mobile campaign commander Gao Zengsheng struck the rebellious Qiang and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Salt Marsh route commander Gao Zengsheng defeated the rebellious Qiang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔：民貲分三等未盡其詳，宜分九等。

translations.literal: On gengyin, an edict stated: The people's property divided into three grades does not exhaust the detail—it should be divided into nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, an edict ordered that the three-tier system of classifying households by wealth was too coarse and should be expanded to nine grades.

sentences.zh: 上謂魏徵曰：「齊後主、周天元皆重斂百姓，厚自奉養，力竭而亡。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wei Zheng, "The Later Lord of Qi and Emperor Xuán of Northern Zhou both heavily levied the people and richly provided for themselves; their strength exhausted, they perished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Wei Zheng, "The Later Lord of Qi and Emperor Xuán of Northern Zhou both taxed the people heavily and lived in lavish self-indulgence until their strength was exhausted and their dynasties fell.

sentences.zh: 譬如饞人自□敢其肉，肉盡而斃，何其愚也！

translations.literal: It is like a glutton devouring his own flesh—when the flesh is gone he dies; how foolish!
translations.idiomatic: They were like gluttons devouring their own flesh—when the flesh was gone they died. How foolish!

sentences.zh: 然二主孰為優劣？

translations.literal: Yet which of the two rulers was superior or inferior?
translations.idiomatic: Yet which of the two was the worse ruler?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「齊後主懦弱，政出多門；

translations.literal: " He replied, "The Later Lord of Qi was weak; government issued from many gates;
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "The Later Lord of Qi was weak; power leaked through many hands;

sentences.zh: 周天元驕暴，威福在己；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuán of Northern Zhou was arrogant and violent; authority and blessings rested in himself;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuán was arrogant and brutal; he kept all power in his own hands;

sentences.zh: 雖同為亡國，齊主尤劣也。

translations.literal: although both alike ruined their states, the Lord of Qi was especially inferior.
translations.idiomatic: though both destroyed their states, the Lord of Qi was the worse of the two.

sentences.zh: 夏，閏四月，癸酉，任城王道宗敗吐谷渾於庫山。

translations.literal: In summer, the intercalary fourth month, on guiyou, the Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Ku.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the intercalary fourth month, on guiyou, the Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Ku.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾可汗伏允悉燒野草，輕兵走入磧。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun qaghan Fuyun burned all the wild grasses and with light troops fled into the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun qaghan Fuyun burned every patch of grass and fled deep into the desert with a lightly equipped force.

sentences.zh: 諸將以為「馬無草，疲瘦，未可深入。

translations.literal: The generals thought, "The horses have no grass and are worn thin—it is not yet possible to penetrate deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The generals argued that with no fodder the horses were gaunt and thin and that a deep pursuit was impossible.

sentences.zh: 」侯君集曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Hou Junji said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Hou Junji said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 向者段志玄軍還，才及鄯州，虜已至其城下。

translations.literal: Previously when Duan Zhixuan's army returned it had barely reached Shazhou when the barbarians were already at the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Zhixuan's army returned earlier, the enemy had reached Shazhou before his men even got back.

sentences.zh: 蓋虜猶完實，眾為之用故也。

translations.literal: This was because the barbarians were still intact and solid and the multitude served them.
translations.idiomatic: That was because the enemy was still intact and their people still followed them willingly.

sentences.zh: 今一敗之後，鼠逃鳥散，斥候亦絕，君臣攜離，父子相失，取之易於拾芥。

translations.literal: Now after one defeat they flee like rats and scatter like birds; scouts too are cut off; ruler and ministers are estranged; fathers and sons lose one another—taking them will be easier than picking up a mustard seed.
translations.idiomatic: Now, after a single defeat, they scatter like rats and birds; their scouts have vanished; ruler and ministers are estranged and fathers and sons separated—capturing them will be easier than picking up a mustard seed.

sentences.zh: 此而不乘，後必悔之。

translations.literal: If this opportunity is not seized, one will surely regret it afterward.
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to seize this moment, we will surely regret it later.

sentences.zh: 」李靖從之。

translations.literal: " Li Jing followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Jing agreed.

sentences.zh: 中分其軍為兩道：靖與薛萬均、李大亮由北道，君集與任城王道宗由南道。

translations.literal: He divided the army in two: Li Jing with Xue Wanjun and Li Daliang by the northern route; Hou Junji with the Prince of Rencheng by the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: The army was split in two: Li Jing, Xue Wanjun, and Li Daliang took the northern route; Hou Junji and the Prince of Rencheng took the southern route.

sentences.zh: 戊子，靖部將薛孤兒敗吐谷渾於曼頭山，斬其名王，大獲雜畜，以充軍食。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Li Jing's subordinate general Xue Gu'er defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Mantou, beheaded their famous king, and captured large numbers of mixed livestock to supply army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Li Jing's subordinate Xue Gu'er defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Mantou, killed one of their senior chieftains, and seized large herds of livestock to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，靖等敗吐谷渾於牛心堆，又敗諸赤水原。

translations.literal: On guisi, Li Jing and the others defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Niuxin and again defeated them at Chishui Plain.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Li Jing defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Niuxin and again at Chishui Plain.

sentences.zh: 侯君集、任城王道宗引兵行無人之境二千餘里，盛夏降霜，經破邏真谷，其地無水，人齕冰，馬啖雪。

translations.literal: Hou Junji and the Prince of Rencheng led troops through trackless country more than two thousand li; in the height of summer frost fell; passing through Poluo Valley there was no water—men gnawed ice and horses ate snow.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji and the Prince of Rencheng marched more than two thousand li through uninhabited land; frost fell in midsummer; in Poluo Valley there was no water, and men chewed ice while horses ate snow.

sentences.zh: 五月，追及伏允於烏海，與戰，大破之，獲其名王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they overtook Fuyun at Wuhai, joined battle, and routed him, capturing his famous king.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they caught Fuyun at Wuhai, routed his army in battle, and captured one of his senior chieftains.

sentences.zh: 薛萬均、薛萬徹又敗天柱王於寺海。

translations.literal: Xue Wanjun and Xue Wanche again defeated the King of the Pillar of Heaven at Sihai.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wanjun and Xue Wanche also defeated the King of the Pillar of Heaven at Sihai.

sentences.zh: 上皇自去秋得風疾，庚子，崩於垂拱殿。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor had suffered a wind ailment since last autumn; on gengzi he died in Chuigong Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor had suffered a stroke the previous autumn; on gengzi he died in Chuigong Hall.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，群臣請上准遺誥視軍國大事，上不許。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the ministers asked that the emperor be permitted to handle state and military affairs according to the testamentary edict; he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, the ministers asked that the emperor be allowed to govern according to the Retired Emperor's deathbed instructions, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔太子承乾於東宮平決庶政。

translations.literal: On yisi, an edict ordered Crown Prince Chengan to settle ordinary government at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, an edict ordered Crown Prince Chengan to handle routine affairs of government from the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 赤水之戰，薛萬均、薛萬徹輕騎先進，為吐谷渾所圍，兄弟皆中槍，失馬步鬥，從騎死者什六七，左領軍將軍契苾何力將數百騎救之，竭力奮擊，所向披靡，萬均、萬徹由是得免。

translations.literal: In the Battle of Red Water, Xue Wanjun and Xue Wanche with light cavalry advanced first, were surrounded by the Tuyuhun; both brothers were struck by spears, lost their horses and fought on foot; of their followers six or seven in ten died; Left Mobile Guard General Qibi Heli led several hundred horsemen to rescue them, exerting his strength in fierce attack, wherever he turned none could stand before him, and Wanjun and Wanche thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Red Water, Xue Wanjun and Xue Wanche led the light cavalry in the van and were surrounded by the Tuyuhun; both brothers were speared and lost their horses, fighting on foot while six or seven tenths of their escort were killed. Left Mobile Guard General Qibi Heli led several hundred horsemen to their rescue, fighting with all his strength until nothing could stand in his way, and the Xue brothers escaped.

sentences.zh: 李大亮敗吐谷渾於蜀渾山，獲其名王二十人。

translations.literal: Li Daliang defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Shuhun and captured twenty of their famous kings.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang defeated the Tuyuhun at Mount Shuhun and took twenty senior Tuyuhun chieftains prisoner.

sentences.zh: 將軍執失思力敗吐谷渾於居茹川。

translations.literal: General Zhisi Sili defeated the Tuyuhun at the Juru River.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhisi Sili defeated the Tuyuhun on the Juru River.

sentences.zh: 李靖督諸軍經積石山河源，至且末，窮其西境。

translations.literal: Li Jing supervised the armies through Jishi Mountain and the River Source to Qiemo, reaching the limits of their western marches.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing led the combined armies through Jishi Mountain and the source of the Yellow River to Qiemo, pushing to the farthest western reaches of Tuyuhun territory.

sentences.zh: 聞伏允在突倫川，將奔于闐，契苾何力欲追襲之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Fuyun was at Tulun River about to flee to Khotan, Qibi Heli wished to pursue and strike him.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Fuyun was at the Tulun River preparing to flee to Khotan, Qibi Heli wanted to pursue and strike him.

sentences.zh: 薛萬均懲其前敗，固言不可。

translations.literal: Xue Wanjun, chastened by his earlier defeat, firmly said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wanjun, mindful of his earlier defeat, insisted they should not go on.

sentences.zh: 何力曰：「虜非有城郭，隨水草遷徙，若不因其聚居襲取之，一朝雲散，豈得復傾其巢穴邪！

translations.literal: Heli said, "The barbarians have no walls or towns; they move with grass and water—if we do not strike while they are gathered together, once they scatter like clouds in a morning how can we again overturn their nest and lair!
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli said, "The enemy have no walled cities; they roam with the grass and water. If we do not strike while they are still gathered, once they scatter like morning clouds, how will we ever uproot their encampments again!

sentences.zh: 」自選驍騎千餘，直趣突倫川，萬均乃引兵從之。

translations.literal: " He himself selected more than a thousand elite horsemen and drove straight for Tulun River; Wanjun then led troops and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: " He picked out more than a thousand of his best horsemen and raced straight for the Tulun River, and Wanjun led his troops after him.

sentences.zh: 磧中乏水，將士刺馬血飲之。

translations.literal: In the desert there was no water; officers and soldiers pierced their horses and drank the blood.
translations.idiomatic: Water ran out in the desert, and the officers and men pierced their horses and drank the blood.

sentences.zh: 襲破伏允牙帳，斬首數千級，獲雜畜二十餘萬，伏允脫身走，俘其妻子。

translations.literal: They raided and broke Fuyun's royal encampment, beheading several thousand; they captured more than two hundred thousand mixed livestock; Fuyun escaped by himself and fled; they took captive his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed and destroyed Fuyun's royal encampment, taking several thousand heads and more than two hundred thousand head of livestock. Fuyun slipped away and fled, but his wife and children were captured.

sentences.zh: 侯君集等進逾星宿川，至柏海，還與李靖軍合。

translations.literal: Hou Junji and the others advanced beyond Xingsu River, reached Baihai, returned, and joined Li Jing's army.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji and the others pushed on beyond the Xingsu River to Baihai, then turned back and united with Li Jing's army.

sentences.zh: 大寧王順，隋氏之甥、伏允之嫡子也，為侍子於隋，久不得歸，伏允立它子為太子，及歸，意常怏怏。

translations.literal: Prince of Daning Shun was a nephew of the Sui house and Fuyun's eldest son by the principal wife; he had served as a court hostage in Sui and long could not return; Fuyun had established another son as crown prince; when he returned, his mind was always resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Daning Shun was a nephew of the Sui imperial house and Fuyun's eldest son by his principal wife. He had long served as a hostage at the Sui court and could not return home; Fuyun had meanwhile made another son his heir. When Shun finally came back, he was constantly aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 會李靖破其國，國人窮蹙，怨天柱王；

translations.literal: It happened that Li Jing broke their state; the people were driven to extremity and blamed the King of the Pillar of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Just then Li Jing shattered their state; the people were brought to ruin and blamed the King of the Pillar of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 順因眾心，斬天柱王，舉國請降。

translations.literal: Shun, following the people's hearts, beheaded the King of the Pillar of Heaven, and the whole state requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shun seized on the popular mood, executed the King of the Pillar of Heaven, and the whole realm offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 伏允帥千餘騎逃磧中，十餘日，眾散稍盡，為左右所殺。

translations.literal: Fuyun led more than a thousand horsemen and fled into the desert; after more than ten days his followers scattered until nearly none remained, and he was killed by those close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun fled into the desert with a little more than a thousand horsemen; after ten-odd days his followers had scattered almost to nothing, and his own companions killed him.

sentences.zh: 國人立順為可汗。

translations.literal: The people of the state established Shun as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun installed Shun as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 壬子，李靖奏平吐谷渾。

translations.literal: On renzi, Li Jing memorialized that Tuyuhun had been pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Li Jing reported that Tuyuhun had been pacified.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔復其國，以慕容順為西平郡王、趉故呂烏甘豆可汗。

translations.literal: On yimao, an edict restored their state, making Murong Shun Prince of Xiping and Wu Gandou Qaghan of Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, an edict restored the Tuyuhun state and made Murong Shun Prince of Xiping and Wu Gandou Qaghan of Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 上慮順未能服其眾，仍命李大亮將精兵數千為其聲援。

translations.literal: The emperor feared Shun might be unable to win over his people and still ordered Li Dalian to lead several thousand picked troops as his supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried that Shun might not be able to command his people and therefore ordered Li Dalian to lead several thousand elite troops as a backing force.

sentences.zh: 六月，己丑，群臣復請聽政，上許之，其細務仍委太子，太子頗能聽斷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jichou, the officials again requested that he resume hearing government; the emperor consented; minor affairs were still entrusted to the crown prince, and the crown prince was quite able to hear cases and decide them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jichou, the officials again asked the emperor to resume governing, and he agreed. Routine business was still left to the crown prince, who proved quite capable of hearing and deciding cases.

sentences.zh: 是後上每出行幸，常令居守監國。

translations.literal: After this, whenever the emperor went out on tour, he always had the crown prince remain behind to guard the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever the emperor traveled, he regularly left the crown prince behind as regent.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚子，鹽澤道行軍副總管劉德敏擊叛羌，破之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengzi, Liu Demin, deputy mobile campaign commander on the Salt Marsh route, struck rebellious Qiang and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengzi, Liu Demin, deputy commander on the Salt Marsh route, attacked rebellious Qiang forces and routed them.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔：「山陵依漢長陵故事，務存隆厚。

translations.literal: On dingsi, an edict said, "The imperial tomb shall follow the precedent of Han's Changling, striving to preserve grandeur and fullness.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, an edict declared, "The imperial tomb shall follow the precedent of the Han Changling, and every effort shall be made to give it solemn grandeur.

sentences.zh: 」期限既促，功不能及。

translations.literal: " The deadline was already urgent, and the work could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: " But the deadline was tight, and the work could not be finished in time.

sentences.zh: 秘書監虞世南上疏，以為：「聖人薄葬其親，非不孝也，深思遠慮，以厚葬適足為親之累，故不為耳。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Yu Shinan submitted a memorial, saying, "Sages bury their parents simply—not from lack of filial piety, but from deep thought and far-reaching concern, knowing that lavish burial only becomes a burden to the parents, and therefore they do not do it.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Yu Shinan submitted a memorial arguing that "sages give their parents simple burials not from lack of filial piety, but from foresight: lavish tombs only become a burden to the dead, and for that reason they refuse them.

sentences.zh: 昔張釋之言：『使其中有可欲，雖錮南山猶有隙。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhang Shizhi said, 'If within it there is something desirable, even if the Southern Mountain were encased in metal there would still be a gap.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shizhi once said, 'If a tomb holds anything worth taking, even a coffin sealed in bronze within Mount Zhongnan would still be broken open.'

sentences.zh: 』劉向言：『死者無終極而國家有廢興，釋之之言，為無窮計也。

translations.literal: ' Liu Xiang said, 'The dead have no end, yet states rise and fall; Zhang Shizhi's words were planning for the infinite.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Liu Xiang said, 'The dead know no end, but dynasties rise and fall; Zhang Shizhi's words were counsel for all time.'

sentences.zh: 』其言深切，誠合至理。

translations.literal: ' Their words were profound and penetrating, truly matching ultimate principle.
translations.idiomatic: ' Their words cut to the heart of the matter and truly accord with right principle.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下聖德度越唐、虞，而厚葬其親乃以秦、漢為法，臣竊為陛下不取。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's sage virtue surpasses Tang and Yu, yet to bury your parent lavishly and take Qin and Han as model—I privately deem this unworthy of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue surpasses even the sage rulers Tang and Yu, yet to bury your father in lavish style after the example of Qin and Han is, I venture, unworthy of you.

sentences.zh: 雖復不藏金玉，後世但見丘壟如此其大，安知其中無金玉邪！

translations.literal: Even if gold and jade are not stored within, later ages seeing a mound so large—how would they know there is no gold and jade inside!
translations.idiomatic: Even if no gold or jade is placed inside, later generations seeing so vast a mound—how will they know the tomb holds nothing worth stealing!

sentences.zh: 且今釋服已依霸陵，而丘壟之制獨依長陵，恐非所宜。

translations.literal: Moreover, now the end of mourning already follows Baling, yet the mound system alone follows Changling—I fear this is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the mourning rites already follow the modest precedent of Baling, while the tomb alone follows the grand scale of Changling—this, I fear, is inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 伏願依《白虎通》為三仞之墳，器物制度，率皆節損，仍刻石立之陵旁，別書一通，藏之宗廟，用為子孫永久之法。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that according to the Baihutong a tomb mound of three ren be made, that implements and regulations all be reduced and economized, that stone still be carved and set beside the tomb, and that another copy be written and stored in the ancestral temple, to serve as a permanent law for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the mound be built three ren high according to the Baihutong, that grave goods and ritual provisions all be scaled back, that an inscription be carved and set beside the tomb, and that a second copy be kept in the ancestral temple as a permanent rule for your descendants.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，不報。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 世南復上疏，以為：「漢天子即位即營山陵，遠者五十餘年；

translations.literal: Shinan again submitted a memorial, saying, "Han emperors upon accession immediately began planning imperial tombs—some as much as fifty-odd years in advance;
translations.idiomatic: Shinan submitted another memorial, noting that "Han emperors began planning their tombs as soon as they took the throne—sometimes fifty years or more before death;

sentences.zh: 今以數月之間為數十年之功，恐於人力有所不逮。

translations.literal: now to accomplish in a few months work meant for decades—I fear human labor will not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: to compress decades of work into a few months, I fear, will exceed what human labor can accomplish.

sentences.zh: 」上乃以世南疏授有司，令詳處其宜。

translations.literal: " The emperor then handed Shinan's memorial to the responsible offices and ordered them to consider in detail what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then referred Shinan's memorial to the relevant offices and ordered them to work out a suitable plan.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡等議，以為：「漢長陵高九丈，原陵高六丈，今九丈則太崇，三仞則太卑，請依原陵之制。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and others deliberated, saying, "Han Changling was nine zhang high, Yuanling six zhang; now nine zhang would be too lofty, three ren too low—we request following Yuanling's system.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and others recommended that "Changling stood nine zhang high and Yuanling six zhang; nine zhang would be too tall and three ren too low—we propose following the Yuanling standard.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，詔：「國初草創，宗廟之制未備，今將遷祔，宜令禮官詳議。

translations.literal: On xinhai, an edict said, "At the founding of the state things were newly established and the ancestral temple system was not complete; now we are about to transfer and enshrine the tablets—the ritual officials should deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, an edict declared, "In the founding years the ancestral temple system was still incomplete; now that the late emperor's tablet is to be installed, the ritual officials should consider the matter carefully.

sentences.zh: 」諫議大夫朱子奢請立三昭三穆而虛太祖之位。

translations.literal: " Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee Zhu Zishe requested establishing three zhao and three mu while leaving the place of the Grand Ancestor vacant.
translations.idiomatic: " Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee Zhu Zishe proposed three zhao and three mu shrines, with the place of the Grand Ancestor left vacant.

sentences.zh: 於是增修太廟，祔弘農府君及高祖並舊神主四為六室。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Grand Ancestral Temple was expanded and repaired; the Lord of Hongnong and Gaozu were enshrined together with the four former spirit tablets, making six chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestral Temple was then enlarged and refurbished; the Lord of Hongnong and Gaozu were enshrined together with the four existing spirit tablets, making six chambers in all.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡等議以涼武昭王為始祖。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and others deliberated that Liang Wuzhaowang should be the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and others proposed making Liang Wuzhaowang the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 左庶子於志寧議以為武昭王非王業所因，不可為始祖；

translations.literal: Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent Yu Zhining deliberated that Wuzhaowang was not the source from which royal enterprise arose and could not be the founding ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent Yu Zhining argued that Wuzhaowang was not the source of the dynasty's rise to power and could not serve as founding ancestor;

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 党項寇疊州。

translations.literal: The Tangut raided Die Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut raided Die Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李靖之擊吐谷渾也，厚賂党項，使為鄉導。

translations.literal: When Li Jing struck Tuyuhun, he richly bribed the Tangut to serve as local guides.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing marched against Tuyuhun, he paid the Tangut handsomely to serve as guides.

sentences.zh: 党項酋長拓跋赤辭來，謂諸將曰：「隋人無信，喜暴掠我。

translations.literal: Tangut chieftain Tuoba Chici came and said to the generals, "Sui people are faithless and delight in violently plundering us.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut chieftain Tuoba Chici came before the generals and said, "The Sui were faithless and loved to raid us by force.

sentences.zh: 今諸軍苟無異心，我請供其資糧；

translations.literal: Now if the various armies have no divergent intent, I request to supply their provisions;
translations.idiomatic: If your armies mean us no harm, I will supply your provisions;

sentences.zh: 如或不然，我將據險以塞諸軍之道。

translations.literal: if otherwise, I will hold the strategic passes and block the armies' routes.
translations.idiomatic: but if not, I will hold the defiles and block your line of march.

sentences.zh: 」諸將與之盟而遣之。

translations.literal: " The generals made alliance with him and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals swore an alliance with him and let him go.

sentences.zh: 赤水道行軍總管李道彥行至闊水，見赤辭無備，襲之，獲牛羊數千頭。

translations.literal: Red Water route mobile campaign commander Li Daoyan reached Kuoshui, saw Chici unguarded, raided him, and captured several thousand head of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Red Water route commander Li Daoyan reached the Kuoshui River, found Chici off his guard, and raided him, seizing several thousand head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 於是群羌怨怒，屯野狐峽，道彥不得進；

translations.literal: Thereupon the Qiang tribes were resentful and angry, encamped at Yehu Gorge, and Daoyan could not advance;
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang tribes were enraged, massed at Yehu Gorge, and Daoyan could not get through;

sentences.zh: 赤辭擊之，道彥大敗，死者數萬，退保松州。

translations.literal: Chici struck him; Daoyan was greatly defeated; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands; he withdrew and held Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chici attacked him and routed his army; tens of thousands were killed, and Daoyan fell back to defend Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 左驍衛將軍樊興逗遛失軍期，士卒失亡多。

translations.literal: Left Mobile Guard General Fan Xing dawdled and missed the army rendezvous; many soldiers were lost or killed.
translations.idiomatic: Left Mobile Guard General Fan Xing had dawdled and missed the rendezvous, and many of his men were lost.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，道彥、興皆坐減死徙邊。

translations.literal: On yimao, Daoyan and Xing were both sentenced for their crimes to commuted death and exile to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Daoyan and Xing were both sentenced to commuted death and exile to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 上遣使勞諸將於大斗拔谷，薛萬均排毀契苾何力，自稱己功。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to comfort the generals at Databo Valley; Xue Wanjun disparaged Qibi Heli and claimed the merit as his own.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to reward the generals at Databo Valley. There Xue Wanjun belittled Qibi Heli and claimed the credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 何力不勝忿，拔刀起，欲殺萬均，諸將救止之。

translations.literal: Heli could not contain his rage; he drew his sword and rose, wishing to kill Wanjun; the generals rescued and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Heli was overcome with fury; he drew his sword and rose to kill Wanjun, but the other generals restrained him.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，以讓何力，何力具言其狀，上怒，欲解萬均官以授何力，何力固辭，曰：「陛下以臣之故解萬均官，群胡無知，以陛下為重胡輕漢，轉相誣告，馳競必多。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and rebuked Heli; Heli fully explained the circumstances; the emperor grew angry and wished to dismiss Wanjun from office and give the post to Heli; Heli firmly declined, saying, "If Your Majesty dismisses Wanjun from office on my account, the various Hu are ignorant and will take Your Majesty to favor Hu and slight Han; they will turn and accuse one another, and frantic rivalry will surely multiply.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he reproached Heli; Heli gave a full account of what had happened. The emperor grew angry and wanted to strip Wanjun of his office and give it to Heli, but Heli firmly refused, saying, "If Your Majesty dismisses Wanjun on my account, the frontier tribes will take it as proof that you favor the Hu over the Han. Accusations will fly back and forth, and jealous rivalry will only multiply.

sentences.zh: 且使胡人謂諸將皆如萬均，將有輕漢之心。

translations.literal: Moreover, it would make the Hu think all the generals are like Wanjun, and they will have a mind to slight the Han.
translations.idiomatic: It would also teach the tribes to think every Tang general is like Wanjun, and they will begin to look down on the Han.

sentences.zh: 」上善之而止。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved this and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his reasoning and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 尋令宿衛北門，檢校屯營事，尚宗女臨洮縣主。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to garrison and guard the north gate and inspect camp affairs, and was given Princess of Lintao County, daughter of Shangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Heli was assigned to garrison the north gate and oversee camp affairs, and was given in marriage Princess Lintao, daughter of Shangzong.

sentences.zh: 岷州都督、鹽澤道行軍總管高甑生後軍期，李靖按之。

translations.literal: Min Prefecture Protector-General and Salt Marsh route mobile campaign commander Gao Zengsheng was late for the army rendezvous; Li Jing investigated him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zengsheng, Protector-General of Min Prefecture and commander on the Salt Marsh route, arrived late for the rendezvous, and Li Jing investigated the offense.

sentences.zh: 甑生恨靖，誣告靖謀反，按驗無狀。

translations.literal: Zengsheng hated Jing and falsely accused him of plotting rebellion; investigation found no substance.
translations.idiomatic: Zengsheng bore a grudge against Li Jing and falsely accused him of treason, but the investigation found no evidence.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚辰，甑生坐減死徙邊。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengchen, Zengsheng was sentenced for his crime to commuted death and exile to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengchen, Zengsheng was sentenced to commuted death and exile to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 或言：「甑生，秦府功臣，寬其罪。

translations.literal: Someone said, "Zengsheng is a meritorious minister of the Prince of Qin's household—be lenient with his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged leniency: "Zengsheng is an old companion from the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「甑生違李靖節度，又誣其反，此而可寬，法將安施！

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Zengsheng disobeyed Li Jing's command and also falsely accused him of rebellion—if this can be leniently treated, where will law be applied!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "Zengsheng defied Li Jing's command and then falsely accused him of treason. If that can be forgiven, what use is the law!

sentences.zh: 且國家自起晉陽，功臣多矣，若甑生獲免，則人人犯法，安可復禁乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, since the state rose from Jinyang there have been many meritorious ministers; if Zengsheng is exempted, then everyone will violate the law—how can it again be forbidden!
translations.idiomatic: Since we rose from Jinyang, we have had many meritorious men. If Zengsheng goes unpunished, every man will break the law—how then can we enforce discipline!

sentences.zh: 我於舊勳，未嘗忘也，為此不敢赦耳。

translations.literal: I have never forgotten old merit—it is for this that I dare not pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: I have not forgotten old service; it is precisely because I remember it that I dare not pardon him.

sentences.zh: 」李靖自是闔門杜絕賓客，雖親戚不得妄見也。

translations.literal: " From this Li Jing closed his gates and cut off guests; even relatives could not see him casually.
translations.idiomatic: " From that time on Li Jing shut his gates to visitors; even kinsmen could not see him without cause.

sentences.zh: 上欲自詣園陵，群臣以上哀毀羸瘠，固諫而止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to go in person to the garden tomb; the officials, because the emperor's grief had wasted him to emaciation, firmly remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to visit the tomb park in person, but the officials, seeing how grief had worn him to skin and bone, firmly dissuaded him and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙亥，處月初遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yihai, Chuyue first sent envoys to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yihai, Chuyue sent tribute envoys to court for the first time.

sentences.zh: 處月、處密，皆西突厥之別部也。

translations.literal: Chuyue and Chumi were both separate divisions of the Western Türks.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyue and Chumi were both branches of the Western Türks.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，葬太武皇帝於獻陵，廟號高祖；

translations.literal: On gengyin, Emperor Taiwu was buried at Xianling; his temple name was Gaozu;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Emperor Taiwu was buried at Xianling and given the temple name Gaozu;

sentences.zh: 以穆皇后祔葬，加號太穆皇后。

translations.literal: Empress Mu was buried with him in joint interment, and her title was augmented to Grand Empress Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Mu was buried with him, and her title was raised to Grand Empress Mu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚戌，詔議於太原立高祖廟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengxu, an edict ordered deliberation on establishing a Gaozu temple at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengxu, an edict ordered discussion of establishing a temple to Gaozu at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 秘書監顏師古議，以為：「寢廟慶在京師，漢世郡國立廟，非禮。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Yan Shigu deliberated, saying, "The resting temple and celebratory rites belong in the capital; Han-era commanderies and kingdoms establishing temples was not ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Yan Shigu argued that "the imperial resting temple and its rites belong in the capital; for commanderies and kingdoms to maintain separate temples, as in Han times, is not proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以光祿大夫蕭瑀為特進，復令參預政事。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Palace Attendant Grandee Xiao Yu was made Special Advance and again ordered to participate in governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Palace Attendant Grandee Xiao Yu was made Special Advance and again invited to take part in government.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「武德六年以後，高祖有廢立之心而未定，我不為兄弟所容，實有功高不賞之懼。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "After the sixth year of Wude, Gaozu had a mind to depose and establish but had not decided; I was not tolerated by my brothers and truly had the fear that merit too high goes unrewarded—or worse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "After the sixth year of Wude, Gaozu was still weighing whether to replace the heir, and my brothers would not tolerate me. I truly feared the old proverb that no reward is great enough for a man whose service has grown too dangerous.

sentences.zh: 斯人也，不可以利誘，不可以死脅，真社稷臣也！

translations.literal: This man cannot be enticed by profit, cannot be coerced by death—he is truly a minister of the altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: This is a man who cannot be bought with profit or broken with threats of death—a true pillar of the state!

sentences.zh: 」因賜瑀詩曰：「疾風知勁草，板蕩識誠臣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he bestowed on Yu a poem saying, "A fierce wind reveals the tough grass; turmoil reveals the loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave Yu a poem: "Only in a fierce wind do you know the tough grass; only in upheaval do you know the loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 」又謂瑀曰：「卿之忠直，古人不過；

translations.literal: " He also said to Yu, "Your loyalty and uprightness— the ancients did not surpass it;
translations.idiomatic: " He also told Yu, "Your loyalty and blunt honesty surpass the ancients;

sentences.zh: 然善惡太明，亦有時而失。

translations.literal: yet to distinguish good and evil too clearly also has times when one errs.
translations.idiomatic: but to judge good and evil too sharply also has its costs.

sentences.zh: 」瑀再拜謝。

translations.literal: " Yu bowed twice in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu bowed twice in acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 魏徵曰：「瑀違眾孤立，唯陛下知其忠勁，向不遇聖明，求免難矣！

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said, "Yu defied the crowd and stood alone; only Your Majesty knew his loyal strength—had he not met a sage and enlightened ruler, he would have sought exemption from disaster in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "Yu stood alone against the court; only Your Majesty recognized his loyal steadfastness. Without a sage ruler, he would never have escaped ruin!

sentences.zh: 特進李靖上書，請依遺誥，御常服，臨正殿；

translations.literal: Special Advance Li Jing submitted a letter requesting that, according to the final testament, the emperor wear ordinary dress and attend the main hall;
translations.idiomatic: Special Advance Li Jing submitted a memorial asking that, in accordance with the late emperor's final testament, the emperor resume ordinary dress and hold court in the main hall;

sentences.zh: 弗許。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾甘豆可汗久質中國，國人不附，竟為其下所殺。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun Gandou Qaghan had long been a hostage in the Central Realm; the people of the state did not attach themselves to him, and in the end he was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shun, the Tuyuhun Gandou Qaghan, had long been a hostage at the Tang court; his people never accepted him, and in the end his own followers killed him.

sentences.zh: 子燕王諾曷缽立。

translations.literal: His son, Prince of Yan Nuohobo, was established.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince of Yan Nuohobo, was installed in his place.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽幼，大臣爭權，國中大亂。

translations.literal: Nuohobo was young; great ministers contended for power, and the state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohobo was still a child; the great ministers fought for power, and the realm descended into chaos.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔兵部尚書侯君集等將兵援之；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict ordered Minister of War Hou Junji and others to lead troops to aid them;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, an edict ordered Minister of War Hou Junji and others to march to their aid;

sentences.zh: 先遣使者諭解，有不奉詔者，隨宜討之。

translations.literal: envoys were first dispatched to instruct and reconcile; those who did not obey the edict were to be punished as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: envoys were sent ahead to explain the imperial will and urge reconciliation; any who refused the edict were to be punished as the situation demanded.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲午，上始親聽政。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiawu, the emperor for the first time personally heard government.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiawu, the emperor resumed personal rule.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以突厥拓設阿史那社爾為左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Türk tuo-she Ashina She'er was made Grand General of the Left Mobile Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the Türk tuo-she Ashina She'er was appointed Grand General of the Left Mobile Guard.

sentences.zh: 社爾，處羅可汗之子也，年十一，以智略聞。

translations.literal: She'er was the son of Qaghan Chuluo; at eleven years of age he was known for strategy and planning.
translations.idiomatic: She'er was a son of Qaghan Chuluo; even at eleven he was already known for his strategic mind.

sentences.zh: 可汗以為拓設，建牙於磧北，與欲谷設分統敕勒諸部，居官十年，未嘗有所賦斂。

translations.literal: The qaghan made him tuo-she; he established his banner north of the desert and, with Yugu she, divided command over the various Tiele tribes; he held office ten years and never imposed any levies or exactions.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan appointed him tuo-she; he raised his banner north of the desert and, together with Yugu she, divided rule over the Tiele tribes. He held the post for ten years without ever imposing a levy.

sentences.zh: 諸設或鄙其不能為富貴，社爾曰：「部落苟豐，於我足矣。

translations.literal: Some tuo-she despised him for not enriching himself; She'er said, "If the tribes are prosperous, that is enough for me.
translations.idiomatic: Some of the other tuo-she looked down on him for failing to enrich himself, but She'er said, "If my tribes are prosperous, that is enough for me.

sentences.zh: 」諸設慚服。

translations.literal: " The tuo-she were ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " The other tuo-she were shamed into respect.

sentences.zh: 及薛延陀叛，攻破欲谷設，社爾兵亦敗，將其餘眾走保西陲。

translations.literal: When Xueyantuo rebelled, they broke Yugu she; She'er's army was also defeated, and he led his remaining followers to flee and hold the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Xueyantuo rebelled, they overran Yugu she and defeated She'er's army as well; he fled west with what remained of his followers.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗既亡，西突厥亦亂，咄陸可汗兄弟爭國。

translations.literal: After Qaghan Jieli perished, the Western Türks also fell into disorder; Qaghan Dulü and his brothers contended for the state.
translations.idiomatic: After Qaghan Jieli's fall, the Western Türks fell into turmoil as Qaghan Dulü and his brothers fought over the khanship.

sentences.zh: 社爾詐往降之，引兵襲破西突厥，取其地幾半，有眾十餘萬，自稱答布可汗。

translations.literal: She'er feigned going to surrender to them, led troops in a surprise attack and broke the Western Türks, took nearly half their territory, had a following of more than one hundred thousand, and styled himself Qaghan Dabou.
translations.idiomatic: She'er pretended to submit, then led a surprise attack that shattered the Western Türks, seized nearly half their territory, gathered more than one hundred thousand followers, and proclaimed himself Qaghan Dabou.

sentences.zh: 社爾乃謂諸部曰：「首為亂破我國者，薛延陀也，我當為先可汗報仇擊滅之。

translations.literal: She'er then said to the various tribes, "The first to rise in disorder and break our state was Xueyantuo; I shall avenge the former qaghan and strike to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: She'er then told the tribes, "Xueyantuo were the first to rise in rebellion and destroy our state. I mean to avenge the former qaghan and wipe them out.

sentences.zh: 」諸部皆諫曰：「新得西方，宜且留鎮撫。

translations.literal: " All the tribes remonstrated, saying, "We have newly gained the west; it is fitting to remain and pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: " The tribes all remonstrated: "We have only just taken the west; you should stay and consolidate it.

sentences.zh: 今遽捨之遠去，西突厥必來取其故地。

translations.literal: Now if we abruptly abandon it and go far away, the Western Türks will surely come and take back their old territory.
translations.idiomatic: If you abandon it now and march far away, the Western Türks will surely return and reclaim their old lands.

sentences.zh: 」社爾不從，擊薛延陀於磧北，連兵百餘日。

translations.literal: " She'er did not follow this; he struck Xueyantuo north of the desert, and the armies were engaged for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: " She'er refused to listen and attacked Xueyantuo north of the desert; the fighting lasted more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 會咥利失可汗立，社爾之眾苦於久役，多棄社爾逃歸。

translations.literal: It happened that Qaghan Yili Shi was established; She'er's followers, worn by long service, mostly abandoned She'er and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Qaghan Yili Shi came to power; She'er's men, exhausted by the long campaign, largely abandoned him and fled home.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀縱兵擊之，社爾大敗，走保高昌，其舊兵在者才萬餘家，又畏西突厥之逼，遂帥眾來降。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo released troops to strike him; She'er suffered a great defeat, fled to hold Gaochang; of his old soldiers who remained there were only a little more than ten thousand households; further fearing pressure from the Western Türks, he then led his followers to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo counterattacked in force; She'er was routed and fled to Gaochang. Fewer than ten thousand households of his original followers remained, and fearing further pressure from the Western Türks, he led his people to submit to Tang.

sentences.zh: 敕處其部落於靈州之北，留社爾於長安，尚皇妹南陽長公主，典屯兵於苑內。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his tribes settled north of Lingzhou; She'er was kept at Chang'an, given in marriage the emperor's younger sister Princess Chang of Nanyang, and put in charge of garrison troops within the park.
translations.idiomatic: An edict settled his tribes north of Lingzhou, kept She'er at Chang'an, married him to the emperor's younger sister, Princess Chang of Nanyang, and put him in charge of the garrison within the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，徙趙王元景為荊王，魯王元昌為漢王，鄭王元禮為徐王，徐王元嘉為韓王，荊王元則為彭王，滕王元懿為鄭王，吳王元軌為霍王，豳王元鳳為虢王，陳王元慶為道王，魏王靈夔為燕王，蜀王恪為吳王，越王泰為魏王，燕王祐為齊王，梁王愔為蜀王，郯王惲為蔣王，漢王貞為越王，申王慎為紀王。

translations.literal: On guichou, Prince of Zhao Yuanjing was moved to Prince of Jing, Prince of Lu Yuanchang to Prince of Han, Prince of Zheng Yuanli to Prince of Xu, Prince of Xu Yuanjia to Prince of Han, Prince of Jing Yuanze to Prince of Peng, Prince of Teng Yuanyi to Prince of Zheng, Prince of Wu Yuangui to Prince of Huo, Prince of Bin Yuanfeng to Prince of Guo, Prince of Chen Yuanqing to Prince of Dao, Prince of Wei Lingqi to Prince of Yan, Prince of Shu Ke to Prince of Wu, Prince of Yue Tai to Prince of Wei, Prince of Yan You to Prince of Qi, Prince of Liang Yin to Prince of Shu, Prince of Tan Yun to Prince of Jiang, Prince of Han Zhen to Prince of Yue, Prince Shen Zhen to Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the emperor reassigned his sons' princely titles: Yuanjing went from Prince of Zhao to Prince of Jing; Yuanchang from Prince of Lu to Prince of Han; Yuanli from Prince of Zheng to Prince of Xu; Yuanjia from Prince of Xu to Prince of Han; Yuanze from Prince of Jing to Prince of Peng; Yuanyi from Prince of Teng to Prince of Zheng; Yuangui from Prince of Wu to Prince of Huo; Yuanfeng from Prince of Bin to Prince of Guo; Yuanqing from Prince of Chen to Prince of Dao; Lingqi from Prince of Wei to Prince of Yan; Ke from Prince of Shu to Prince of Wu; Tai from Prince of Yue to Prince of Wei; You from Prince of Yan to Prince of Qi; Yin from Prince of Liang to Prince of Shu; Yun from Prince of Tan to Prince of Jiang; Zhen from Prince of Han to Prince of Yue; and Shen Zhen from Prince of Shen to Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙丑，以元景為荊州都督，元昌為梁州都督，元禮為徐州都督，元嘉為潞州都督，元則為遂州都督，靈夔為幽州都督，恪為潭州都督，泰為相州都督，祐為齊州都督，愔為益州都督，惲為安州都督，貞為揚州都督。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yichou, Yuanjing was made Superintendent of Jingzhou, Yuanchang Superintendent of Liangzhou, Yuanli Superintendent of Xuzhou, Yuanjia Superintendent of Luzhou, Yuanze Superintendent of Suizhou, Lingqi Superintendent of Youzhou, Ke Superintendent of Tanzhou, Tai Superintendent of Xiangzhou, You Superintendent of Qizhou, Yin Superintendent of Yizhou, Yun Superintendent of Anzhou, and Zhen Superintendent of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yichou, the emperor appointed his sons regional superintendents: Yuanjing to Jingzhou, Yuanchang to Liangzhou, Yuanli to Xuzhou, Yuanjia to Luzhou, Yuanze to Suizhou, Lingqi to Youzhou, Ke to Tanzhou, Tai to Xiangzhou, You to Qizhou, Yin to Yizhou, Yun to Anzhou, and Zhen to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 泰不之官，以金紫光祿大夫張亮，行都督事。

translations.literal: Tai did not take up his post; Palace Attendant Grandee Zhang Liang was ordered to act as superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Tai did not take up his post; Palace Attendant Grandee Zhang Liang was ordered to serve as acting regional superintendent.

sentences.zh: 上以泰好文學，禮接士大夫，特命於其府別置文學館，聽自引召學士。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Tai loved literature and courteously received scholar-officials, specially ordered a separate Literary Academy set up at his residence, allowing him to recruit and summon scholars himself.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tai loved literature and treated scholar-officials with courtesy, the emperor specially ordered a separate Literary Academy established at his princely residence and allowed him to recruit scholars on his own.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁酉，吐谷渾王諾曷缽遣使請頒歷，行年號，遣子弟入侍；

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingyou, the king of Tuyuhun Nuohobo sent envoys requesting the issuance of the calendar and adoption of the reign era, and sending sons and younger brothers to serve at court;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingyou, Nuohobo, king of Tuyuhun, sent envoys asking to receive the imperial calendar, adopt the Tang reign era, and send sons and younger brothers to serve at court;

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted every request.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以諾曷缽為河源郡王、烏地也拔勤豆可汗。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Nuohobo was made Prince of Heyuan Commandery and Qaghan Wudiyebalidou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Nuohobo was enfeoffed as Prince of Heyuan Commandery and given the title Qaghan Wudiyebalidou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，諸王之籓，上與之別曰：「兄弟之情，豈不欲常共處邪！

translations.literal: On guichou, as the princes went out to their fiefs, the emperor took leave of them, saying, "Brotherly affection—would one not wish to stay together always!
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, as the princes departed for their fiefs, the emperor bade them farewell, saying, "Brotherly love—who would not wish to remain together always!

sentences.zh: 但以天下之重，不得不爾。

translations.literal: But given the weight of the realm, one cannot do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: But the burden of the realm leaves no other choice.

sentences.zh: 諸子尚可復有，兄弟不可復得。

translations.literal: Sons one might yet have again; brothers one cannot have again.
translations.idiomatic: One may yet have more sons, but brothers cannot be had again.

sentences.zh: 」因流涕嗚咽不能止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he shed tears and sobbed, unable to stop.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept and sobbed, unable to stop himself.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，壬申，以溫彥博為右僕射，太常卿楊師道為侍中。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, on renshen, Wen Yanbo was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Minister of Ceremonies Yang Shidao was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, on renshen, Wen Yanbo was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Yang Shidao, Minister of Ceremonies, was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 侍中魏徵屢以目疾求為散官，上不得已，以征為特進，仍知門下事，朝章國典，參議得失，徒流以上罪，詳事聞奏；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Wei Zheng repeatedly, on account of eye disease, requested a nominal post; the emperor, having no choice, made Zheng Special Advance, while he still handled affairs of the Chancellery, deliberating on court regulations and state statutes, discussing gains and losses, and for crimes of exile or above, examining matters and reporting to the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Wei Zheng repeatedly asked to be relieved to a nominal post because of eye trouble; the emperor reluctantly made him Special Advance while keeping him in charge of Chancellery affairs—deliberating on court regulations and state law, weighing policy, and reviewing and reporting on cases involving exile or heavier punishments;

sentences.zh: 其祿賜、吏卒並同職事。

translations.literal: His salary, gifts, clerks, and attendants were all the same as for an active post.
translations.idiomatic: His salary, perquisites, clerks, and attendants remained the same as before.

sentences.zh: 長孫皇后性仁孝儉素，好讀書，常與上從容商略古事，因而獻替，裨益弘多。

translations.literal: Empress Changsun was by nature benevolent, filial, frugal, and plain; she loved reading and often discussed ancient affairs at leisure with the emperor, thereby offering corrections and substitutions, to great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Changsun was benevolent, filial, frugal, and plain by nature. She loved books and often discussed historical precedents with the emperor in unhurried conversation, offering counsel that proved of great benefit.

sentences.zh: 上或以非罪譴怒宮人，後亦陽怒，請自推鞫，因命囚系，俟上怒息，徐為申理，由是宮壺之中，刑無枉濫。

translations.literal: When the emperor sometimes condemned and raged at palace women without real offense, the empress also feigned anger, requested to investigate herself, and then ordered them imprisoned; when the emperor's anger subsided, she slowly vindicated them—whereby within the inner palace there was no wrongful punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor unjustly raged at palace women, the empress would feign anger as well, ask to investigate the matter herself, and have them imprisoned; once his anger cooled, she would gradually clear them. In this way no innocent woman in the inner palace suffered wrongful punishment.

sentences.zh: 豫章公主早喪其母，後收養之，慈愛逾於所生。

translations.literal: Princess Yuzhang lost her mother early; the empress took her in and raised her, loving her more than her own child.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Yuzhang had lost her mother at an early age; the empress adopted her and loved her even more tenderly than her own children.

sentences.zh: 妃嬪以下有疾，後親撫視，輟己之藥膳以資之，宮中無不愛戴。

translations.literal: When consorts and those below them fell ill, the empress personally attended them, setting aside her own medicines and food to supply them; none in the palace did not love and revere her.
translations.idiomatic: When consorts and lower-ranking women fell ill, she nursed them herself and gave them her own medicines and food. Everyone in the palace loved and revered her.

sentences.zh: 訓諸子，常以謙儉為先，太子乳母遂安夫人嘗白後，以東宮器用少，請奏益之。

translations.literal: In instructing her sons, she always put humility and frugality first. The crown prince's wet nurse, Lady Sui'an, once reported to the empress that the Eastern Palace had too few utensils and requested a memorial to increase them.
translations.idiomatic: In raising her sons she always put humility and thrift first. The crown prince's wet nurse, Lady Sui'an, once told the empress that the Eastern Palace had too few furnishings and asked her to petition for more.

sentences.zh: 後不許，曰：「為太子，患在德不立，名不揚，何患無器用邪！

translations.literal: The empress did not permit it, saying, "For a crown prince, the worry is that virtue is not established and fame is not spread—what worry is there about lacking utensils!
translations.idiomatic: The empress refused, saying, "For a crown prince, the danger lies in virtue unestablished and reputation unearned—what need is there to worry over furnishings!

sentences.zh: 上得疾，累年不愈，後侍奉，晝夜不離側。

translations.literal: The emperor fell ill and for years did not recover; the empress attended him, day and night never leaving his side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell ill and for years did not recover; the empress nursed him day and night, never leaving his side.

sentences.zh: 常系毒藥於衣帶，曰：「若有不諱，義不獨生！

translations.literal: She often tied poison to her belt, saying, "If there should be the unspeakable, by right I shall not live alone!
translations.idiomatic: She kept poison tied to her belt, saying, "If the worst should come, I cannot in conscience outlive him!

sentences.zh: 」後素有氣疾，前年從上幸九成宮，柴紹等中夕告變，上擐甲出閣問狀，後扶疾以從，左右止之，後曰：「上既震驚，吾何心自安！

translations.literal: " The empress had long suffered from a breathing ailment; the year before last she accompanied the emperor on a visit to Jiucheng Palace. Chai Shao and others reported a disturbance at midnight; the emperor donned armor and went out of the pavilion to inquire; the empress, supporting herself despite illness, followed. Those at her side tried to stop her; the empress said, "The emperor is already alarmed—how could my heart be at ease alone!
translations.idiomatic: " The empress had long suffered from a breathing ailment. Two years earlier, when she accompanied the emperor to Jiucheng Palace, Chai Shao and others reported a disturbance at midnight. The emperor donned armor and rushed out to investigate; though ill, the empress insisted on following. Attendants tried to stop her, but she said, "The emperor is already shaken—how can I rest easy alone!

sentences.zh: 」由是疾遂甚。

translations.literal: " Thereby her illness then grew severe.
translations.idiomatic: " Her illness worsened sharply as a result.

sentences.zh: 太子言於後曰：「醫藥備盡而疾不瘳，請奏赦罪人及度人入道，庶獲冥福。

translations.literal: The crown prince said to the empress, "Medicine has been fully tried yet the illness is not cured; I request a memorial to pardon criminals and ordain people into the Way, hoping thereby to obtain hidden blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince told the empress, "Every remedy has been tried, yet she does not recover. I wish to petition for a general pardon and for people to be ordained as Daoist or Buddhist clergy, hoping this may win divine favor.

sentences.zh: 」後曰：「死生有命，非智力所移。

translations.literal: " The empress said, "Life and death have their allotted span; they are not moved by wit or strength.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress replied, "Life and death are fated; no wit or effort can alter them.

sentences.zh: 若為善有福，則吾不為惡；

translations.literal: If doing good brings blessing, then I have not done evil;
translations.idiomatic: If virtue truly brings blessing, then I have not lived wickedly;

sentences.zh: 如其不然，妄求何益！

translations.literal: if it is not so, what use is vain seeking!
translations.idiomatic: if not, what good can empty prayers do!

sentences.zh: 赦者國之大事，不可數下。

translations.literal: Amnesty is a great matter of state and cannot be issued repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty is a grave matter of state and must not be proclaimed again and again.

sentences.zh: 道、釋異端之教，蠹國病民，皆上素所不為，奈何以吾一婦人使上為所不為乎？

translations.literal: The Way and Buddhism are heterodox teachings that harm the state and afflict the people—all things the emperor has never done; how can I, one woman, make the emperor do what he has never done?
translations.idiomatic: Daoism and Buddhism are heterodox faiths that drain the state and harm the people—things the emperor has always refused. How can I, one woman, make him do what he has always rejected?

sentences.zh: 必行汝言，吾不如速死！

translations.literal: If you must carry out your words, I would rather die quickly!
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on this, I would rather die at once!

sentences.zh: 」太子不敢奏，私以語房玄齡，玄齡白上，上哀之，欲為之赦，後固止之。

translations.literal: " The crown prince did not dare memorialize; he privately told Fang Xuanling, and Xuanling reported to the emperor. The emperor was moved with pity and wished to grant the amnesty for her sake, but the empress firmly stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince did not dare submit the petition; he told Fang Xuanling in private, and Xuanling reported it to the emperor. Moved to pity, the emperor wished to grant the amnesty for her sake, but the empress firmly forbade it.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，與上訣。

translations.literal: When her illness grew critical, she took leave of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When her illness turned critical, she bade the emperor farewell.

sentences.zh: 時房玄齡以譴歸第，後言於上曰：「玄齡事陛下久，小心慎密，奇謀秘計，未嘗宣洩，苟無大故，願勿棄之。

translations.literal: At the time Fang Xuanling had returned home under censure; the empress said to the emperor, "Xuanling has served Your Majesty long, careful and discreet; his strange plans and secret stratagems have never been divulged. If there is no great cause, I hope you will not cast him aside.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling had then been sent home under censure. The empress told the emperor, "Xuanling has served you long with careful discretion; his secret counsel has never been leaked. Unless he has committed some grave fault, do not cast him aside.

sentences.zh: 妾之本宗，因緣葭莩，以致祿位，既非德舉，易致顛危，欲使其子孫保全，慎勿處之權要，但以外戚奉朝請足矣。

translations.literal: My own clan, through the bond of distant kin by marriage, attained salary and rank; it was not by virtue that we were raised, and disaster comes easily. To keep their descendants secure, take care not to place them in posts of power; let them serve merely as affinal kin attending court—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: My own clan rose through distant marriage ties, not merit, and such fortune invites ruin. To keep my family's descendants safe, never place them in posts of power; let them remain mere affinal kin attending court, and that will be enough.

sentences.zh: 妾生無益於人，不可以死害人，願勿以丘壟勞費天下，但因山為墳，器用瓦木而已。

translations.literal: In life I benefited no one; in death I must not harm others. I wish you not to burden the realm with tomb mounds and expense; merely take a hill for the grave, with utensils of tile and wood only.
translations.idiomatic: I benefited no one in life and must not burden others in death. Do not exhaust the realm over my tomb; let a hillside suffice for my grave, with only earthenware and wood for furnishings.

sentences.zh: 仍願陛下親君子，遠小人，納忠諫，屏讒慝，省作役，止游畋，妾雖沒於九泉，誠無所恨！

translations.literal: I still wish Your Majesty to be close to gentlemen, keep petty men at a distance, accept loyal remonstrance, shut out slander and wickedness, reduce corvée labor, and stop roaming hunts—then though I sink into the nine springs, truly I shall have no regret!
translations.idiomatic: I still ask that you draw close to the worthy, keep the base at a distance, heed loyal counsel, shut out slander and malice, lighten corvée burdens, and stop pleasure hunts. Then though I lie beneath the earth, I shall have no regret!

sentences.zh: 兒女輩不必令來，見其悲哀，徒亂人意。

translations.literal: The sons and daughters need not be summoned; to see their grief would only disturb people's hearts in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Do not summon the children; their grief would only unsettle everyone to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 」因取衣中毒藥以示上曰：「妾於陛下不豫之日，誓以死從乘輿，不能當呂後之地耳。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she took the poison from her garment and showed it to the emperor, saying, "On the days when Your Majesty was unwell, I vowed to follow the imperial carriage in death—I cannot occupy the place of Empress Lü.
translations.idiomatic: " She then took the poison from her robe and showed it to him, saying, "When Your Majesty was ill, I swore to follow you in death. I cannot play the part of Empress Lü.

sentences.zh: 」己卯，崩於立政殿。

translations.literal: " On jimao she passed away in Lizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " On jimao she died in Lizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 後嘗采自古婦人得失事，為《女則》三十卷，又嘗著論駁漢明德馬後以不能抑退外親，使當朝貴盛，徒戒其車如流水馬如龍，是開其禍敗之源而防其末流也。

translations.literal: The empress once gathered accounts from antiquity of women's gains and losses and compiled them into thirty juan of Lessons for Women; she also once wrote a treatise refuting Later Han Empress Mingde Ma for failing to restrain and dismiss affinal kin, allowing them to become noble and powerful at court—merely warning against carriages like flowing water and horses like dragons was opening the source of disaster and ruin while guarding only the final current.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had once collected stories of women's successes and failures from antiquity and compiled them into thirty juan of Lessons for Women. She also wrote a treatise criticizing Later Han's Empress Mingde Ma for failing to restrain her affinal kin, allowing them to dominate the court: to warn only against lavish carriages and horses was to leave the source of ruin untouched while policing its last effects.

sentences.zh: 及崩，宮司並《女則》奏之，上覽之悲慟，以示近臣曰：「皇后此書，足以垂范百世！

translations.literal: When she passed away, the palace offices together presented Lessons for Women; the emperor read it and was grieved and stricken, showing it to close ministers and saying, "The empress's book is enough to serve as a model for a hundred generations!
translations.idiomatic: After her death the palace offices presented Lessons for Women together with her memorial rites. The emperor read it, stricken with grief, and showed it to his closest ministers, saying, "This book of the empress's is a model for a hundred generations!

sentences.zh: 朕非不知天命而為無益之悲，但入宮不復聞規諫之言，失一良佐，故不能忘懷耳！

translations.literal: It is not that I do not know Heaven's mandate yet indulge useless grief, but that entering the palace I no longer hear words of remonstrance—I have lost a fine assistant, and therefore cannot forget!
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I do not know fate when I grieve uselessly, but that within the palace I no longer hear her counsel—I have lost a fine adviser, and cannot put her from my mind!

sentences.zh: 」乃召房玄齡，使復其位。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he summoned Fang Xuanling and restored him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: " He then recalled Fang Xuanling and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，丙子，上謂群臣曰：「朕開直言之路，以利國也，而比來上封事者多訐人細事，自今復有為是者，朕當以讒人罪之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on bingzi, the emperor said to the assembled ministers, "I opened the path of blunt speech to benefit the state, yet recently those submitting sealed memorials mostly expose people's petty affairs. From now on, if any do this again, I shall treat them as slanderers.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on bingzi, the emperor told the assembled ministers, "I opened the way for blunt speech to serve the state, yet lately sealed memorials have mostly been petty attacks on individuals. From now on, anyone who does this again I shall treat as a slanderer.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，庚午，葬文德皇后於昭陵。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on gengwu, Empress Wende was buried at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on gengwu, Empress Wende was interred at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 將軍段志玄、宇文士及分統士眾出肅章門。

translations.literal: Generals Duan Zhixuan and Yuwen Shiji separately commanded soldiers and went out through Suchang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Duan Zhixuan and Yuwen Shiji commanded separate detachments of troops out through Suchang Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝夜使宮官至二人所，士及開營內之；

translations.literal: At night the emperor sent palace officials to the two men's camps; Shiji opened the camp and admitted them;
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor sent palace officials to both camps; Shiji opened his camp and admitted them;

sentences.zh: 志玄閉門不納，曰：「軍門不可夜開。

translations.literal: Zhixuan closed the gate and would not admit them, saying, "The army gate cannot be opened at night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixuan shut the gate and refused them entry, saying, "An army gate must not be opened at night.

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「此有手敕。

translations.literal: " The envoy said, "Here is a handwritten edict.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy said, "I bear a handwritten edict from the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」志玄曰：「夜中不辨真偽。

translations.literal: " Zhixuan said, "In the middle of the night one cannot distinguish true from false.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhixuan replied, "In the dark of night one cannot tell true from false.

sentences.zh: 」竟留使者至明。

translations.literal: " In the end he kept the envoy until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: " He kept the envoy waiting until dawn.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而歎曰：「真將軍也！

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and sighed, saying, "A true general!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he sighed and said, "There is a true general!

sentences.zh: 帝復為文刻之石，稱「皇后節儉，遺言薄葬，以為『盜賊之心，止求珍貨，既無珍貨，復何所求。

translations.literal: The emperor again had an inscription carved in stone, stating, "The empress was frugal; her final words were for a plain burial," reasoning, "Thieves' hearts seek only precious goods; if there are no precious goods, what more is there to seek?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also had an inscription carved in stone, noting the empress's frugality and her wish for a plain burial. He wrote, "Thieves seek only treasure; without treasure, what is left to steal?

sentences.zh: 』朕之本志，亦復如此。

translations.literal: ' My original intent is likewise so.
translations.idiomatic: ' That has always been my own intent as well.

sentences.zh: 王者以天下為家，何必物在陵中，乃為己有。

translations.literal: A king takes the realm as his home—why must objects be in the tomb before they are considered his own?
translations.idiomatic: A ruler makes the realm his home; why must possessions lie in a tomb before they are truly his?

sentences.zh: 今因九嵕山為陵，鑿石之工才百餘人，數十日而畢。

translations.literal: Now, taking Jiufeng Mountain for the tomb, the stone-cutting workers numbered only a little more than a hundred men, and in several tens of days it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: We have taken Jiufeng Mountain for the tomb; barely more than a hundred stonecutters were employed, and the work was finished in a few dozen days.

sentences.zh: 不藏金玉，人馬、器皿，皆用土木，形具而已，庶幾奸盜息心，存沒無累。

translations.literal: No gold or jade is stored; men, horses, and vessels are all of earth and wood, form alone—that is all—so that perhaps evil thieves will quiet their hearts, and the living and dead be unburdened.
translations.idiomatic: No gold or jade is buried there; figures of men, horses, and vessels are made only of earth and wood, mere forms. Thus thieves should lose interest, and neither the living nor the dead be burdened.

sentences.zh: 當使百世子孫奉以為法。

translations.literal: This should make a hundred generations of descendants take it as law.
translations.idiomatic: Let a hundred generations of descendants take this as their model.

sentences.zh: 上念後不已，於苑中作層觀以望昭陵，嘗引魏徵同登，使視之。

translations.literal: The emperor's longing for the empress did not cease; in the park he built a multi-storied pavilion to gaze upon Zhaoling, and once led Wei Zheng up with him and had him look.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not stop grieving for the empress. In the park he built a multi-storied pavilion from which to view Zhaoling, and once brought Wei Zheng up with him to look.

sentences.zh: 征熟視之曰：「臣昏眊，不能見。

translations.literal: Zheng looked carefully and said, "Your servant is dim-sighted and cannot see.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng studied the view carefully and said, "I am too dim of sight to make it out.

sentences.zh: 」上指示之，征曰：「臣以為陛下望獻陵若昭陵，則臣固見之矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor pointed it out to him; Zheng said, "Your servant believes that if Your Majesty looked upon Xian Mausoleum as you look upon Zhaoling, then your servant would indeed see it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor pointed it out; Zheng said, "If Your Majesty looked upon Xian Mausoleum as you look upon Zhaoling, then I would certainly see it.

sentences.zh: 」上泣，為之毀觀。

translations.literal: " The emperor wept and had the pavilion destroyed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wept and had the pavilion torn down.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊寅，朱俱波、甘棠遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, Zhujubo and Gantang sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, Zhujubo and Gantang sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 朱俱波在蔥嶺之北，去瓜州三千八百里。

translations.literal: Zhujubo lies north of the Onion Mountains, thirty-eight hundred li from Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhujubo lay north of the Pamirs, thirty-eight hundred li from Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 甘棠在大海南。

translations.literal: Gantang is south of the Great Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Gantang lay south of the Great Sea.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「中國既安，四夷自服。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Since the Central Realm is already at peace, the four barbarians naturally submit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Now that the realm is at peace, the four quarters submit of themselves.

sentences.zh: 然朕不能無懼，昔秦始皇威振胡、越，二世而亡，唯諸公匡其不逮耳。

translations.literal: Yet I cannot be without fear. Formerly Qin Shihuang's might shook the Hu and Yue, yet the Second Generation perished—only you gentlemen can correct what I fail to reach.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I cannot help but fear. Qin Shihuang once made the northern and southern peoples tremble, yet his dynasty fell in the second generation. It is for you gentlemen to remedy what I lack.

sentences.zh: 魏王泰有寵於上，或言三品以上多輕魏王。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Tai had the emperor's favor; someone said that officials of the third rank and above mostly looked down on Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Tai enjoyed the emperor's favor; someone reported that many officials of the third rank and above looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 上怒，引三品以上，作色讓之曰：「隋文帝時，一品以下皆為諸王所頓躓，彼豈非天子兒邪！

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, summoned those of the third rank and above, changed countenance, and reproached them, saying, "In Emperor Wen of Sui's time, all below the first rank were trampled by the princes—were they not sons of the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, summoned all officials of the third rank and above, and rebuked them sternly: "Under Emperor Wen of Sui, princes trampled everyone below the first rank—were they not also sons of the emperor!

sentences.zh: 朕但不聽諸子縱橫耳，聞三品以上皆輕之，我若縱之，豈不能折辱公輩乎！

translations.literal: I merely do not allow my sons to run rampant—that is all. Hearing that all of the third rank and above look down on him, if I let them run rampant, could I not humiliate you gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: I simply refuse to let my sons run wild—that is all. If I hear that you all look down on him, and if I were to indulge them, could they not humiliate every one of you!

sentences.zh: 」房玄齡等皆惶懼流汗拜謝。

translations.literal: " Fang Xuanling and the others were all fearful, sweating, and bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: " Fang Xuanling and the others broke into a fearful sweat and bowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 魏徵獨正色曰：「臣竊計當今群臣，心無敢輕魏王者。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng alone, with upright countenance, said, "Your servant privately reckons that among the ministers today, in heart none dare look down on Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng alone, unflinching, said, "I do not believe any minister today would dare look down on Prince of Wei in his heart.

sentences.zh: 在禮，臣、子一也。

translations.literal: In ritual, minister and son are one.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual propriety, a minister and a son occupy the same position.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》：王人雖微，序於諸侯之上。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals: though a royal envoy be humble, he is ranked above the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals ranks even the humblest royal envoy above the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 三品以上皆公卿，陛下所尊禮，若紀綱大壞，固所不論；

translations.literal: Those of the third rank and above are all high ministers whom Your Majesty honors and treats with ritual; if the great norms were utterly broken, that would be another matter;
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the third rank and above are the high ministers Your Majesty himself honors; if the court's order were utterly broken, that would be another matter;

sentences.zh: 聖明在上，魏王必無頓辱群臣之理。

translations.literal: with sage illumination above, Prince of Wei surely has no reason to trample and humiliate the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: but with a sage ruler above, Prince of Wei has no grounds to humiliate the ministers.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝驕其諸子，使多行無禮，卒皆夷滅，又足法乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui indulged his sons, letting them often act without propriety, and in the end they were all exterminated—is that worth taking as model?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui spoiled his sons until they behaved without restraint, and in the end they were all destroyed—is that a precedent worth following?

sentences.zh: 」上悅，曰：「理到之語，不得不服。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased and said, "Words that reach to principle—one cannot but submit.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased and said, "When reason is put so plainly, one cannot but yield.

sentences.zh: 朕以私愛忘公義，向者之忿，自謂不疑，及聞征言，方知理屈。

translations.literal: I, through private affection, forgot public right; in my earlier anger I thought myself without doubt, but on hearing Zheng's words I then knew my reason was bent.
translations.idiomatic: Private affection made me forget public duty. In my anger I had thought myself in the right, but hearing Zheng I knew I was in the wrong.

sentences.zh: 人主發言何得容易乎！

translations.literal: How can a ruler's words be spoken lightly!
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's words cannot be spoken lightly!

sentences.zh: 上曰：「法令不可數變，數變則煩，官長不能盡記；

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Laws and orders cannot be changed repeatedly; if changed repeatedly they become burdensome, and officials cannot fully remember them;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Laws must not be changed too often; frequent changes make them burdensome, and officials cannot keep them all in mind;

sentences.zh: 又前後差違，吏得以為奸。

translations.literal: furthermore, when earlier and later versions differ, clerks are able to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: and when successive versions contradict one another, clerks find room for abuse.

sentences.zh: 自今變法，皆宜詳慎而行之。

translations.literal: From now on, in changing laws, all should be carried out with thorough care.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, every change in law must be enacted with thorough care.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史權萬紀上言：「宣、饒二州銀大發采之，歲可得數百萬緡。

translations.literal: Imperial Secretary Attendant Censor Quan Wanji submitted a statement: "In Xuan and Rao prefectures silver has been discovered in great abundance; if mined, each year several million strings of cash could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Secretary Attendant Censor Quan Wanji memorialized: "Rich silver deposits have been found in Xuan and Rao prefectures; mining them could yield several million strings of cash each year.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕貴為天子，所乏者非財也，但恨無嘉言可以利民耳。
