translations.literal: " The emperor said, "I am exalted as Son of Heaven; what I lack is not wealth, but I regret that there are no fine words by which to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I am emperor; what I lack is not wealth, but good counsel that truly benefits the people.

sentences.zh: 與其多得數百萬緡，何如得一賢才！

translations.literal: Rather than gaining several million strings more, how does that compare with gaining one worthy talent!
translations.idiomatic: What is several million strings of cash compared with finding one worthy man!

sentences.zh: 卿未嘗進一賢，退一不肖，而專言稅銀之利。

translations.literal: You have never advanced one worthy man or dismissed one unworthy, yet you speak exclusively of the profit of taxing silver.
translations.idiomatic: You have never recommended one worthy man or urged the removal of one unfit, yet you speak only of the profit to be had from silver taxes.

sentences.zh: 昔堯、舜抵璧於山，投珠於谷，漢之桓、靈乃聚錢為私藏，卿欲以桓、靈俟我邪！

translations.literal: Formerly Yao and Shun cast jade disks against mountains and threw pearls into valleys; Han's Huan and Ling amassed money for private hoards—you wish to make me await comparison with Huan and Ling!
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun cast jade disks against mountains and threw pearls into valleys; the Han emperors Huan and Ling hoarded money for themselves. Do you mean to rank me with Huan and Ling!

sentences.zh: 」是日。

translations.literal: " That same day,
translations.idiomatic: " That same day,

sentences.zh: 黜萬紀，使還家。

translations.literal: Wanji was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Wanji was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 是歲，更命統軍為折衝都尉，別將為果毅都尉。

translations.literal: That year, [they] renamed army commanders as Charge-and-Smash Commandants and separate commanders as Determined-Fruit Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: That year the title of army commander was changed to Charge-and-Smash Commandant, and that of deputy commander to Determined-Fruit Commandant.

sentences.zh: 凡十道，置府六百三十四，而關內二百六十一，皆隸諸衛及東宮六率。

translations.literal: In ten circuits in all, 634 garrisons were established; of these 261 were within the passes, all subordinate to the various guards and the Eastern Palace's six commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Ten circuits in all had 634 garrisons established, 261 of them in the interior passes—all subordinate to the guard commands and the Eastern Palace's six commanderies.

sentences.zh: 凡上府兵千二百人，中府千人，下府八百人。

translations.literal: Upper garrisons had 1,200 soldiers, middle garrisons 1,000, and lower garrisons 800.
translations.idiomatic: Upper garrisons fielded 1,200 men, middle garrisons 1,000, and lower garrisons 800.

sentences.zh: 三百人為團，團有校尉；

translations.literal: Three hundred men formed a regiment, and each regiment had a company commander;
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred men made a regiment, each with its own company commander;

sentences.zh: 五十人為隊，隊有正；

translations.literal: fifty men formed a platoon, and each platoon had a squad leader;
translations.idiomatic: fifty men made a platoon, each with a squad leader;

sentences.zh: 十人為火，火有長。

translations.literal: ten men formed a squad, and each squad had a chief.
translations.idiomatic: ten men made a squad, each with a squad chief.

sentences.zh: 每人兵甲糧裝各有數，皆自備，輸之庫，有征行則給之。

translations.literal: Each man had a fixed allotment of armor, weapons, provisions, and equipment; all were self-supplied, deposited in the storehouse, and issued when there was a campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Each man was allotted a fixed set of armor, weapons, provisions, and gear—all supplied by himself, deposited in the storehouse, and issued out when troops were sent on campaign.

sentences.zh: 年二十為兵，六十而免。

translations.literal: At age twenty one became a soldier; at sixty one was released.
translations.idiomatic: Men entered service at twenty and were discharged at sixty.

sentences.zh: 其能騎射者為越騎，其餘為步兵。

translations.literal: Those able to ride and shoot became cross-country cavalry; the rest became foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could ride and shoot were assigned to the mounted cross-country corps; the rest served as infantry.

sentences.zh: 每歲季冬，折衝都尉帥其屬教戰，當給馬者官予其直市之。

translations.literal: Every year in the last month of winter, Charge-and-Smash Commandants led their subordinates in drill; for those who should be given horses, the government gave their price to buy them.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in late winter the Charge-and-Smash Commandants drilled their men; those due to receive horses were given cash by the government to buy them on the market.

sentences.zh: 凡當宿衛者番上，兵部以遠近給番，遠疏、近數，皆一月而更。

translations.literal: All who were to serve as palace guards rotated on duty; the Ministry of War assigned rotations according to distance—distant [regions] with sparse shifts, near [regions] with frequent shifts—all changing every month.
translations.idiomatic: All palace-guard duty rotated by turn; the Ministry of War set the roster by distance—the farther away, the less frequent the shift; the nearer, the more frequent—with every man relieved after one month.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，徙鄶王元裕為鄧王，譙王元名為舒王。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Prince of Zan Yuan Yu was moved to Prince of Deng, and Prince of Qiao Yuan Ming to Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Prince Yuan Yu of Zan was reassigned as Prince of Deng, and Prince Yuan Ming of Qiao as Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以吳王恪為安州都督，晉王治為并州都督，紀王慎為秦州都督。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Prince Wu Ke was made Area Commander of Anzhou, Prince Jin Zhi of Bingzhou, and Prince Ji Shen of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Prince Ke of Wu was appointed area commander of An Prefecture, Prince Zhi of Jin of Bing Prefecture, and Prince Shen of Ji of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 將之官，上賜書戒敕曰：「吾欲遺汝珍玩，恐益驕奢，不如得此一言耳。

translations.literal: As they were about to take up their posts, the emperor bestowed letters of admonition, saying: "I wish to leave you precious curios, but fear they would only increase pride and extravagance; better to leave you this one sentence alone.
translations.idiomatic: As they set out for their posts the emperor gave them letters of warning: "I could send you precious treasures, but I fear that would only feed your pride and extravagance. One word from me is worth more.

sentences.zh: 上作飛山宮。

translations.literal: The emperor built Feishan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built Feishan Palace.

sentences.zh: 庚子，特進魏徵上疏，以為：「煬帝恃其富強，不虞後患，窮奢極欲，使百姓困窮，以至身死人手，社稷為墟。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Privy Counselor Wei Zheng submitted a memorial, stating: "Emperor Yang relied on his wealth and power, gave no thought to later troubles, exhausted extravagance and extreme desire, drove the common people to distress and poverty, until he himself fell to another's hand and the altars of state became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Privy Counselor Wei Zheng memorialized: "Emperor Yang trusted in wealth and strength, never foresaw the reckoning to come, pushed extravagance to the extreme, and drove the people into want—until he died by another's hand and the dynasty was left in ruins.

sentences.zh: 陛下撥亂返正，宜思隋之所以失，我之所以得，撤其峻宇，安於卑宮；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has put chaos to rights and restored proper order; you should reflect on how Sui lost and how we gained, dismantle lofty halls, and dwell in humble palaces;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has turned chaos back to order; you should ponder why Sui fell and why we rose, tear down towering halls, and be content with modest dwellings;

sentences.zh: 若因基而增廣，襲舊而加飾，此則以亂易亂，殃咎必至，難得易失，可不念哉！

translations.literal: if on the existing foundations you expand and enlarge, following the old and adding ornament, then you will exchange one disorder for another; disaster is bound to come—what is hard to win is easy to lose—can you fail to keep this in mind!
translations.idiomatic: If you build on existing foundations and expand them, follow old patterns and add ornament, you will only replace one kind of ruin with another. Calamity is sure to follow—what was hard won is easily lost. Can Your Majesty afford to forget this!

sentences.zh: 房玄齡等先受詔定律令，以為：「舊法，兄弟異居，廕不相及，而謀反連坐皆死；

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and others, having earlier received orders to codify laws and statutes, held that: "Under the old law, brothers living apart were not implicated by hereditary privilege, yet in cases of treason and rebellion all linked by guilt were put to death;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and others, earlier charged to compile the laws and statutes, argued: "Under the old code, brothers who lived separately were not implicated by privilege of office, yet everyone implicated in treason was put to death;

sentences.zh: 祖孫有廕，而止應配流。

translations.literal: when grandparents and grandchildren had hereditary privilege, they should only be sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: while grandparents and grandchildren who held hereditary privilege merited only exile.

sentences.zh: 據禮論情，深為未愜。

translations.literal: Considered by ritual and human feeling, this was deeply unsatisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: By the standards of ritual and human sympathy, this was deeply unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 今定律，祖孫與兄弟緣坐者俱配役。

translations.literal: Now in fixing the law, grandparents and grandchildren and brothers linked by guilt are all sentenced to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: The new code provides that grandparents, grandchildren, and brothers linked by guilt shall all be sentenced to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 自是比古死刑，除其太半，天下稱賴焉。

translations.literal: From this time compared with antiquity, capital punishment was reduced by more than half; the realm acclaimed and relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: From this time on, compared with ancient practice, executions were cut by more than half—and the realm rejoiced in it.

sentences.zh: 玄齡等定律五百條，立刑名二十等，比隋律減大辟九十二條，減流入徙者七十一條，凡削煩去蠹，變重為輕者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Xuanling and others fixed five hundred articles of law, establishing twenty grades of punishment by name; compared with Sui law, capital crimes were reduced by ninety-two articles, exile and hard labor by seventy-one; in all, cutting away complexity and removing corruption, turning heavy into light—too many to count.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling and his colleagues codified five hundred articles and twenty grades of punishment. Compared with Sui law, they struck ninety-two capital offenses and seventy-one crimes punishable by exile or hard labor. Simplifications and lightenings beyond count.

sentences.zh: 又定令一千五百九十餘條。

translations.literal: They also fixed more than 1,590 articles of ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: They also set more than 1,590 administrative ordinances.

sentences.zh: 武德舊制，釋奠於太學，以周公為先聖，孔子配饗；

translations.literal: Under the old Wude system, at the libation sacrifice in the Imperial Academy, the Duke of Zhou was honored as primary sage and Confucius was secondary in the offering;
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Wude regulations, the Imperial Academy's sacrifice placed the Duke of Zhou as primary sage with Confucius in secondary place;

sentences.zh: 玄齡等建議停祭周公，以孔子為先聖，顏回配饗。

translations.literal: Xuanling and others recommended ceasing sacrifice to the Duke of Zhou, taking Confucius as primary sage, and Yan Hui as secondary in the offering.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling and his colleagues recommended ending sacrifice to the Duke of Zhou, making Confucius primary sage with Yan Hui as secondary.

sentences.zh: 又刪武德以來敕格，定留七百條，至是頒行之。

translations.literal: They also culled imperial edicts and regulations since Wude, fixing seven hundred to remain; to this point they were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: They also pruned imperial edicts and administrative rules dating back to Wude, retaining seven hundred articles, which were now promulgated.

sentences.zh: 又定枷、杻、鉗、鎖、杖、笞，皆有長短廣狹之制。

translations.literal: They also fixed cangues, shackles, fetters, locks, staffs, and bamboo floggings—all with standards of length, breadth, and width.
translations.idiomatic: They also standardized cangues, shackles, fetters, locks, beating staves, and flogging rods, each with prescribed dimensions.

sentences.zh: 自張蘊古之死，法官以出罪為戒；

translations.literal: Since Zhang Yungu's death, judicial officials took acquittal as a warning;
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhang Yungu's execution, judges treated acquittal as a thing to beware of;

sentences.zh: 時有失入者，又不加罪。

translations.literal: when there were wrongful convictions they likewise went unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: yet wrongful convictions went unpunished as well.

sentences.zh: 上嘗問大理卿劉德威曰：「近日刑網稍密，何也？

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Liu Dewei: "Recently the criminal net has grown somewhat tight—why?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Chief Judge Liu Dewei of the Court of Judicial Review: "Lately the net of criminal justice has tightened—why is that?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此在主上，不在群臣，人主好寬則寬，好急則急。

translations.literal: " He answered: "This lies with the sovereign, not with the officials; if the ruler favors leniency then it is lenient, if he favors severity then it is severe.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "That rests with Your Majesty, not with your ministers. If the ruler favors clemency, the courts are clement; if he favors severity, they are severe.

sentences.zh: 律文：失入減三等，失出減五等。

translations.literal: The text of the law: for wrongful conviction, punishment is reduced three degrees; for wrongful acquittal, five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The law provides that a wrongful conviction reduces the judge's penalty by three degrees; a wrongful acquittal by five.

sentences.zh: 今失入無辜，失出更獲大罪，是以吏各自免，競就深文，非有教使之然，畏罪故耳。

translations.literal: Now wrongful conviction goes unpunished, while wrongful acquittal incurs greater guilt; thus officials each protect themselves, competing to apply harsh interpretations—no one ordered this, they fear guilt, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Today wrongful convictions go unpunished, while wrongful acquittals bring down the heavier penalty. Officials protect themselves and compete to apply the harshest reading of the law—not because anyone orders it, but because they fear punishment.

sentences.zh: 陛下倘一斷以律，則此風立變矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would once for all decide according to law, then this practice would immediately change.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would enforce the law even-handedly, this practice would change overnight.

sentences.zh: 」上悅，從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased and followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased and agreed.

sentences.zh: 由是斷獄平允。

translations.literal: From this, judgments in cases became fair and balanced.
translations.idiomatic: From that time forward, trials were fair and balanced.

sentences.zh: 上以漢世豫作山陵，免子孫蒼猝勞費，又志在儉葬，恐子孫從欲奢靡；

translations.literal: The emperor, because in Han times mountain tombs were prepared in advance—sparing descendants sudden labor and expense—and because he personally wished for a frugal burial, feared that descendants might follow their desires into extravagance;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that in Han times imperial tombs were prepared in advance, sparing heirs sudden expense and toil; he himself wished to be buried simply, yet feared that later generations might indulge their desires in lavish funerals;

sentences.zh: 二月，丁巳，自為終制，因山為陵，容棺而已。

translations.literal: In the second month, on dingsi, he personally made his burial regulations: using the mountain for the tomb, sufficient only to hold the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingsi, he drew up his own funeral code: a tomb hewn from the mountain, large enough for the coffin and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上行幸洛陽宮。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the emperor traveled to Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor traveled to Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 上至顯仁宮，官吏以缺儲偫，有被譴者。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Xianren Palace, officials were punished for shortfalls in stored provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xianren Palace, several officials were punished for insufficient stored provisions.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「陛下以儲偫譴官吏，臣恐承風相扇，異日民不聊生，殆非行幸之本意也。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "Your Majesty punishes officials for stored provisions; I fear that following this wind they will egg one another on, and in time the people will be unable to live—hardly the original intent of travel!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "Your Majesty is punishing officials over stored provisions. I fear others will take the cue, and one day the people will have nothing to live on. That can hardly have been Your Majesty's purpose in traveling!

sentences.zh: 昔煬帝諷郡縣獻食，視其豐儉以為賞罰，故海內叛之。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Yang hinted that prefectures and counties should present food, viewing abundance or scarcity as grounds for reward and punishment; therefore the realm rebelled against him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang once signaled that counties should present food, rewarding or punishing officials according to abundance or scarcity—and the realm turned against him.

sentences.zh: 此陛下所親見，奈何欲效之乎！

translations.literal: This Your Majesty saw with your own eyes—how can you wish to imitate it!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty saw this yourself—how can you mean to imitate it!

sentences.zh: 」上驚曰：「非公不聞此言。

translations.literal: " The emperor started and said: "Without you I would never have heard this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor started: "Without you I would never have heard this said.

sentences.zh: 」因謂長孫無忌等曰：「朕昔過此，買飯而食，僦舍而宿；

translations.literal: " He then said to Zhangsun Wuji and others: "When I passed here before, I bought rice to eat and rented lodging to sleep;
translations.idiomatic: " He then told Zhangsun Wuji and the others: "When I passed through here before, I bought a meal and rented a room for the night;

sentences.zh: 今供頓如此，豈得猶嫌不足乎！

translations.literal: now provisioning is like this—can one still complain it is insufficient!
translations.idiomatic: and now provisioning is like this—how can anyone still say it is not enough!

sentences.zh: 三月，丙戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of bingxu, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the new moon of bingxu, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 庚子，上宴洛陽宮西宛，泛積翠池，顧謂侍臣曰：「煬帝作此宮苑，結怨於民，今悉為我有，正由宇文述、虞世基、裴蘊之徒內為諂諛、外蔽聰明故也，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: On gengzi, the emperor feasted in the western garden of Luoyang Palace, boating on Jicui Pond; turning to his attendant officials he said: "Emperor Yang built this palace and garden, earning the people's resentment; now all of it is mine—precisely because men like Yuwen Shu, Yu Shiji, and Pei Yun within flattered and without blocked clear sight. Can this fail to be a warning!
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the emperor gave a banquet in the western park of Luoyang Palace and drifted on Jicui Pond. He turned to his attendants and said: "Emperor Yang built this palace and park and earned the people's hatred. Now it is all mine—because men like Yuwen Shu, Yu Shiji, and Pei Yun flattered him within and blinded his judgment without. Let that be a warning!

sentences.zh: 房玄齡、魏徵上所定《新禮》一百三十八篇；

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng presented to the emperor the New Rites they had fixed—138 chapters;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng presented the 138 chapters of the New Rites they had compiled;

sentences.zh: 丙午，詔行之。

translations.literal: on bingwu, an edict ordered their implementation.
translations.idiomatic: and on bingwu an edict ordered them put into effect.

sentences.zh: 以禮部尚書王珪為魏王泰師，上謂泰曰：「汝事珪當如事我。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Wang Gui was made tutor to Prince Wei Tai; the emperor told Tai: "In serving Gui you should be as in serving me.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, minister of rites, was appointed tutor to Prince Tai of Wei. The emperor told Tai: "Serve Gui as you would serve me.

sentences.zh: 」泰見珪，輒先拜，珪亦以師道自居。

translations.literal: " When Tai met Gui, he always bowed first; Gui likewise comporting himself according to the teacher's way.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever Tai met Gui he bowed first, and Gui for his part held himself to the full dignity of a teacher.

sentences.zh: 子敬直尚南平公主。

translations.literal: Gui's son Jingzhi married Princess Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's son Jingzhi was betrothed to Princess Nanping.

sentences.zh: 先是，公主下嫁，皆不以婦禮事舅姑，珪曰：「今主上欽明，動循禮法，吾受公主謁見，豈為身榮，所以成國家之美耳。

translations.literal: Previously, when princesses married down, none observed the wife's rites toward parents-in-law. Gui said: "Now the sovereign is discerning and bright, moving always according to ritual and law; that I receive the princess's visit is not for my personal honor, but to complete the realm's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when an emperor's daughter married a subject's household, she did not observe the daughter-in-law's rites toward her parents-in-law. Gui said: "Our sovereign is wise and thorough in ritual. That I accept the princess's visit is not for my personal glory—it is to bring honor to the state.

sentences.zh: 」乃與其妻就席坐，令公主執{□弁}，行盥饋之禮。

translations.literal: " He then with his wife took seats and had the princess hold the ceremonial basket, performing the hand-washing and food-serving rites.
translations.idiomatic: " He and his wife took their seats and had the princess take up the ceremonial basket and perform the hand-washing and food-serving rites for them.

sentences.zh: 是後公主始行婦禮，自珪始。

translations.literal: After this, princesses began to observe the wife's rites—from Gui this began.
translations.idiomatic: From that time, imperial daughters began to observe the daughter-in-law's rites—and the precedent began with Gui.

sentences.zh: 群臣復請封禪，上使秘書監顏師古等議其禮，房玄齡裁定之。

translations.literal: The officials again petitioned for Feng and Shan; the emperor had Secretariat Director Yan Shigu and others discuss the rites, and Fang Xuanling settled them.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers again petitioned for the Feng and Shan sacrifices. The emperor had Secretariat Director Yan Shigu and others discuss the ritual, with Fang Xuanling making the final decisions.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己卯，魏徵上疏，以為：「人主善始者多，克終者寡，豈取之易而守之難乎？

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jimao, Wei Zheng submitted a memorial, stating: "Among rulers, many start well but few finish well—is acquiring easy and keeping hard?
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jimao, Wei Zheng memorialized: "Many rulers begin well, but few end well. Is it that gaining power is easy and keeping it is hard?

sentences.zh: 蓋以殷憂則竭誠以盡下，安逸則驕恣而輕物；

translations.literal: It is because in deep worry one exhausts sincerity to exhaust oneself for inferiors, while in ease and comfort one grows proud and willful and treats things lightly;
translations.idiomatic: It is because in times of peril a ruler gives his whole heart to those below, while in ease and comfort he grows arrogant and careless;

sentences.zh: 盡下則胡、越同心，輕物則六親離德，雖震之以威怒，亦皆貌從而心不服故也。

translations.literal: exhausting oneself for inferiors then Hu and Yue share one heart; treating things lightly then the six kin depart from virtue—even if shaken by awe and anger, all only comply in appearance while the heart is not persuaded.
translations.idiomatic: Give your whole heart to those below and even distant peoples stand with you; grow careless and even kin turn away. Though you may terrify men with wrath, they will obey only outwardly while their hearts rebel.

sentences.zh: 人主誠能見可欲則思知足，將興繕則思知止，處高危則思謙降，臨滿盈則思挹損，遇逸樂則思撙節，在宴安則思後患，防壅蔽則思延納，疾讒邪則思正己，行爵賞則思因喜而僭，施刑罰則思因怒而濫，兼是十思，而選賢任能，固可以無為而治，又何必勞神苦體以代百司之任哉！

translations.literal: If the ruler can truly, seeing what is desirable then think of contentment, about to undertake construction then think of knowing when to stop, standing in high peril then think of humble deference, facing fullness then think of drawing off, encountering ease and pleasure then think of restraint, in feasting and peace then think of later troubles, guarding against obstruction and concealment then think of extending reception, hating slander and wickedness then think of correcting oneself, granting ranks and rewards then think of improper enlargement through joy, imposing punishments then think of improper overflow through anger—hold these ten reflections, and select the worthy and employ the able, then one can govern through non-action. Why must one toil in spirit and weary the body to replace the hundred offices' duties!
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler, seeing temptation, remembers contentment; on the verge of new building, remembers when to stop; standing in peril, remembers humility; facing abundance, remembers restraint; enjoying pleasure, remembers moderation; living in ease, remembers disaster to come; guarding against being walled off, remembers to hear all counsel; hating slander, remembers to examine himself; granting rewards, remembers not to overreach in joy; inflicting punishments, remembers not to exceed in anger—if he keeps these ten reflections in mind, selects the worthy and employs the able, he may govern effortlessly. Why toil body and spirit to do the work of every office himself?
